fd3ff24d021469bb: KUALA LUMPUR: The Road Transport Department (RTD) has suspended vehicle type approval for the Chery Omoda 5 following a viral incident in Johor Baru last week in which the vehicle's rear axle detached completely.
RTD director-general Datuk Aedy Fadly Ramli said the move would also halt new registrations of the model until the technical investigation was completed and potential safety risks identified.

"The action will target the specific models and variants potentially involved. At the same time, Chery Malaysia must identify all potentially affected vehicles based on part numbers, production batches, vehicle identification numbers and other relevant technical parameters.
"A recall must be carried out for all units identified as posing a safety risk for inspection and appropriate corrective action," he said in a statement today.
He added that RTD would conduct a technical audit of the Chery Omoda 5 production and assembly lines, as well as the relevant axle component suppliers.
"The audit will cover compliance with good manufacturing practice, quality control systems, weld joint inspection procedures and the safety of components used."

Aedy Fadly said the department would not compromise on any non-compliance that could endanger road users, adding that manufacturers were responsible for ensuring their vehicles met prescribed safety standards and technical requirements.
"The suspension will only be lifted once all corrective and preventive measures have been fully implemented and RTD has confirmed that all safety risks have been adequately addressed."
cb476a49a16133c9: BUKIT MERTAJAM, Oct 11 — Employers are urged to leverage Job Coach services to help workers with disabilities (PwD) adapt to their duties and work environment, thereby expanding inclusive employment opportunities.

Deputy Minister of Women, Family and Community Development Lim Hui Ying said the services would also help employers understand the needs of PwD workers and adopt appropriate communication methods to ensure they could perform their duties effectively.
She said with appropriate guidance, workplace adjustments and mutual understanding, more persons with disabilities could perform well at work and contribute productively.

“Employers should provide training opportunities, identify their talents and create a fair and safe working environment,” she said when officiating the ‘Langkah Bersama Berapit 2.0: Careers and Opportunities for Youths with Disabilities’ programme here today.

She said the parents’ concerns about the future of their children with disabilities after they completed schooling, including access to skills training and employers’ willingness to hire and guide them, needed to be addressed seriously.

She said differences in communication, learning or social interaction, particularly among neurodivergent youths, including individuals with autism and attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), as well as those with learning difficulties, should not be a barrier to employment opportunities.
Instead, she said, a safe work environment that supports individual needs should be established to enable this group to develop their respective capabilities and potential.

Lim said empowering persons with disabilities requires comprehensive cooperation among ministries, government agencies, training institutions and the private sector to ensure they have access to education, skills training and employment opportunities.
She also encouraged more companies to support these efforts through corporate social responsibility (CSR) programmes and initiatives to recruit PwD workers.
Meanwhile, she said the RM1.5 billion allocation for PwD under Budget 2027 will benefit more than 300,000 recipients.

Among the measures announced was an increase in the monthly Bedridden PwD Care and Chronically Ill Patients Allowance from RM500 to RM600, as well as an increase in the threshold for the Disabled Workers’ Allowance from RM1,700 to RM2,000.
The government also provides free public transport passes to the PwD community, and 3,000 new PwD caregivers will receive specialised skills training.
A total of 15 Community-Based Rehabilitation (PDK) premises will also be upgraded into specialised therapy centres. — Bernama
f8333ba085fdf66d: BANTING, Oct 11 — The Sultan of Selangor, Sultan Sharafuddin Idris Shah, today officiated the renaming of Dataran Morib to Dataran Dato’ Seri Harun Idris at Pantai Morib here.
Also present was the Tengku Permaisuri of Selangor, Tengku Permaisuri Norashikin, while Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari accompanied the Sultan during the ceremony.
The renaming honours the late Datuk Seri Harun Idris, the eighth Selangor Menteri Besar, in recognition of his contributions to the state. He also served as the Morib state assemblyman.

In a statement, Kuala Langat Municipal Council (MPKL) said the square officially reopened to the public today following the completion of the RM60.50 million Morib Beach Conservation Project on July 1.
The federal government project was implemented by the Ministry of Energy Transition and Water Transformation (PETRA) in collaboration with the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (JPS).
According to MPKL, the project was undertaken following a high-tide incident on September 18, 2020, which caused a retaining wall to collapse and damaged the coastal area.
The conservation works included beach nourishment along a 750-metre stretch, construction of a 750-metre seawall, two offshore breakwaters and two beacon lights.
Meanwhile, the Selangor government has allocated RM55 million under the Second Selangor Plan (RS-2) for three coastal conservation projects in Kuala Langat.
Of this amount, RM15 million is allocated for erosion-control structures and beach nourishment at Pantai Kampung Endah (Istana Bahagia).

Another RM20 million will fund erosion-control structures and upgrading of the coastal bund at Pantai Batu Laut, while RM20 million has been allocated for erosion-control structures and beach nourishment at Pantai Tumbuk.
MPKL said the square had also undergone upgrades to its facilities and infrastructure, with the improvements expected to attract more domestic and international tourists. — Bernama
cc9c59f53efbb8cb: KUALA LUMPUR: Despite making a strong start to the race, Moto3 rookie Hakim Danish Ramli was forced to settle for 14th at the Grand Prix of Indonesia after being handed a three second penalty on Sunday.
Danish was involved in a last-lap incident with GRYD Racing's Joel Kelso, who crashed. Stewards found Danish to be at fault and handed him the penalty.
The AEON Credit-MT Helmets-MSI rider had initially crossed the line 12th, though was demoted to 14th following the penalty.
Danish otherwise had a strong race and was in contention to secure a top-10 finish.
The 19-year-old had to start from the back of the grid after being penalised for slow riding during qualifying one on Saturday.

CFMoto Gaviota Aspar Team's Maximo Quiles won the race in 32:36.821s with Liqui Moly Dynavolt Intact GP's David Almansa (+2.994s) and Red Bull KTM Ajo's Brian Uriarte (+5.156s) taking second and third.
4f284ee56dcc561a: KATHMANDU: At least 40 houses and two suspension bridges were swept away by a flash flood on the Kaligandaki River in Nepal's Gorkha district on Sunday morning, a local official said, Xinhua reported.
A landslide blocked the river in Chumanubri Rural Municipality, triggering a flash flood when the blockage gave way.
"At least 40 houses in five different settlements have been swept away by the flood," Laxmi Gurung, vice-chairperson of the rural municipality, said.
No casualties have been reported so far.
Residents living along the river corridor were advised to evacuate their homes early on Sunday following warnings of a possible flood.
Authorities are still gathering details of the damage, Gurung said.
Rescue teams, including personnel dispatched from Kathmandu, have reached the disaster site, while further assessments are under way.
dc55972da7b3ff04: LUMUT, Oct 11 — There is currently no urgent need to evacuate Malaysian students in Saudi Arabia, but close monitoring is being carried out following yesterday’s attack at King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh.

Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir said monitoring was being conducted in several areas, particularly Madinah and Makkah, to prevent any risks that could threaten the students’ safety.

“The crisis in the Middle East has been ongoing for the past seven months. At present, there is no need for an evacuation, but we will work closely with the Foreign Ministry to obtain the latest information from time to time,” he said.
He was speaking to reporters after officiating the Targeted Higher Education Assistance Programme at Dewan Mohd Anwar, TVETMARA, here today.
Yesterday, the Saudi General Authority of Civil Aviation reported that 12 people were killed and 309 injured in the attack at King Khalid International Airport.
The fatalities comprised four Saudi nationals, two Bangladeshis, and one each from the United States, Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Palestine and Sudan.
On the programme, Zambry said RM200,000 had been allocated to 400 selected students from low-income families to help reduce their education costs.

He said the assistance, channelled through Education Malaysia Global Services (EMGS), covered students at public universities, teacher education institutes (IPGs), matriculation colleges, polytechnics and other institutions.
“Each student receives RM500, distributed in stages to ensure the assistance is fully utilised for matters related to their studies,” he said.
He hoped the assistance would help students continue their studies smoothly and ease their families’ financial burden, particularly those with many dependants. — Bernama
e149089a60d2c9bd: KUALA LUMPUR: The Football Association of Malaysia (FAM) has confirmed receipt of the naturalisation application documents for KL City defender Giancarlo Gallifuoco, which are currently being processed by the governing body's secretariat.
FAM president Datuk Ab Ghani Hassan said he had received confirmation from the FAM general secretary regarding the receipt of the documents.
However, Gallifuoco must still undergo several processes before a decision can be made on his application.
"The documents are still at the secretariat stage. I have checked with the general Secretary. Yes, it is true that FAM has received the documents from Gallifuoco.
"However, there are still certain processes that Gallifuoco must go through," he said when met at the Sultans' Gold Cup final at the University of Malaya Arena on Saturday.

Australian Gallifuoco revealed the update via X, noting that his lawyer is handling the naturalisation process and has submitted the relevant documents to FAM for further legal review by the governing body.
If the process for the former Tottenham Hotspur youth player proceeds smoothly and meets all eligibility criteria, Gallifuoco could potentially become a new star for the Harimau Malaya squad.
Intriguingly, Gallifuoco could partner with heritage defender Brad Tapp, who recently impressed with his solid performances for Harimau Malaya at the FIFA Asean Cup.
Tapp played a pivotal role in helping Malaysia finish third and ensured Malaysia's goal remained unbreached throughout the tournament.
Should Gallifuoco also receive the green light to represent the country, a partnership between the two players could offer the coaching staff more options to strengthen the Harimau Malaya defence.
b0ecc23afb1e3c10: SYDNEY: Rescue efforts are under way for 73 passengers stranded aboard the MV Awka in the Solomon Islands after the vessel's engine failed, Xinhua reported.
Aircraft and vessels have been mobilised to deliver essential supplies.
The vessel issued a distress signal at around 7am local time on Friday while travelling from Anuta to Vanikoro in Temotu Province.
The 73 passengers do not include the crew, the Solomon Islands Broadcasting Corporation (SIBC) reported on Saturday.
The MV Awka has been drifting at sea amid rough conditions and high swells, raising concerns about the situation on board, SIBC News reported.

France, Australia and New Zealand have received the distress signal and offered assistance, including food, drinking water and medical supplies, Temotu Province Premier Stanley Tehiahua told SIBC News.

94bf85c4fc85a98c: KUALA LUMPUR: A massage chair presented by Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman to his new wife, actress and singer Bella Astillah, has amused Malaysians after the full-sized piece of furniture was wheeled straight into their wedding ceremony yesterday.
The massage chair was one of seven gift trays presented by Syed Saddiq to Bella during their solemnisation ceremony at Menara Merdeka 118 in Kuala Lumpur.
The unusual choice quickly caught the attention of social media users, who were tickled to see a real, working appliance rather than a miniature model or a photo.
​Shairy Hanapiah, one of the men tasked with carrying the wedding gifts, took to social media to share how he ended up involved in the unexpected assignment.
He revealed that he was not originally on the list of helpers and had missed all the preparations.
​Instead, Shairy received a late-night call from Muda president Amira Aisya at 11.25pm, asking if he could help out the following morning.
An extra pair of hands was urgently needed to push the bulky massage chair into the venue.
​Recalling his reaction when a photograph of the chair landed on his WhatsApp, Shairy admitted he could not stop laughing at Syed Saddiq's choice.
​"What is this MP thinking?" he joked, expressing his surprise that the politician had opted for an actual, heavy-duty massage chair instead of a symbolic token.
​Even though he accepted the job at short notice, Shairy confessed he felt nervous about manoeuvring such a large item through the venue, especially with the event being livestreamed.
To make matters worse, he had no time for a rehearsal.

​"I didn't even get to join any rehearsal. Everything was impromptu! And the rest is history," he wrote, adding that everything went off without a hitch and the funny moment gave Malaysians a good laugh.
​Syed Saddiq later explained that his wedding gifts were chosen with long-term family well-being in mind, focusing on health and financial security.
Along with the massage chair, his seven trays included health and life insurance coverage, a bicycle, a study package, RM100,000 in Employees Provident Fund contributions, and a gym set.
Bella reciprocated with nine trays of gifts for her husband.

The couple tied the knot at 10.40am in a ceremony solemnised by former Federal Territories mufti Datuk Seri Dr Zulkifli Mohamad Al-Bakri. Bella, 32, and Syed Saddiq, 33, exchanged their vows in front of close family and friends, kicking off their new chapter together.
3969b43e8c5dac5d: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 11 — Kota Kinabalu is set to be transformed into a smart city through a project worth about RM300 million, expected to be completed by February 2028, enhancing urban management, public safety and service delivery.

Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said the Kota Kinabalu Smart City Project, which began on August 6, was being implemented through a collaboration between the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and Kota Kinabalu City Hall (DBKK), using Universal Service Provision (USP) funds.

She said the project involved developing fibre-optic and public Wi-Fi networks, including 50 kilometres of backbone network and 308 kilometres of last-mile network, installing 822 smart poles and multi-purpose poles, and establishing a Network Operations Command Centre (NOCC).

A total of 1,696 closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras would also be installed across the DBKK administrative area to enable real-time monitoring of urban activities, strengthening the local authority’s ability to manage traffic, security and emergencies more effectively.
“The function of this smart city is that, by installing CCTV cameras, you can collect real-time data,” she told reporters after inspecting the NOCC development site here today.
Teo said the use of real-time data would enable DBKK to make more accurate and timely decisions, thereby improving urban management and service delivery to residents.

She said the NOCC, housed in the former Kota Kinabalu Magistrates’ Court building, would also give the historic building a new lease of life, with a dedicated data centre being developed next to it to support smart city operations.
The data centre would have a capacity of 120 kilowatts (kW), with an additional 30 kW of reserve capacity, and would be equipped with a backup power supply system to ensure uninterrupted operations.

Teo said renovation works on the NOCC building and construction of the data centre were expected to be completed within six months, after which DBKK staff would undergo training and knowledge transfer in preparation for operating the system.
She said the project also included public Wi-Fi facilities to improve digital connectivity, support local business growth and create new economic opportunities for the community.
Teo said MCMC would bear the operating costs of the smart city infrastructure for five years after the two-year development period, before handing over the entire facility to DBKK.
Meanwhile, Kota Kinabalu MP Datuk Chan Foong Hin described the project as an important step towards transforming Sabah’s state capital into a more modern, safe and competitive smart city.

The Deputy Agriculture and Food Security Minister said the digital infrastructure would not only improve urban management but also enhance the safety of residents and tourists, in line with Kota Kinabalu’s growth as a tourism destination.
“This is a good project because repurposing this heritage building will help position Kota Kinabalu among the cities embracing smart city development,” he said.

Chan said integrating information from the CCTV network and other digital systems would enable authorities to make more accurate predictions on traffic conditions, weather and public safety, improving urban planning and management.

He also expressed his appreciation to MCMC for implementing the project, describing it as a major contribution to Kota Kinabalu’s development, particularly in accelerating Sabah’s digital transformation. — Bernama
6c733e145d7185e1: INDIA'S verification exercise of its nearly one billion voters has sparked protests across the country, with opposition parties alleging the removal of 130 million names from electoral rolls has unfairly benefited Prime Minister Narendra Modi's party.

Election Commission data cited by Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party shows about 130 million names, more than the population of Japan, have been deleted from electoral rolls during the verification exercise, including 63 million people who had relocated and 30 million who could not be traced.

The BJP and the Commission deny allegations of manipulation, although opposition parties say Muslim voters and other minorities, who are unlikely to support the Hindu nationalist ruling party, are disproportionately impacted by the deletions.
They say the deletions have affected the outcome of some recent state elections that the BJP won, and have cast a shadow on the electoral process in the world's biggest democracy.
The voter verification drive has become one of the biggest political controversies of Modi's 12-year tenure ahead of crucial state elections starting early next year.
Supporters of the Cockroach Janta Party youth movement, farmers' groups and opposition parties are set to protest in Delhi on Saturday, demanding the resignation of Kumar.
Police say they have not granted permission, and CJP has reported preemptive detentions of some protest leaders.

Sporadic protests have been going on across India since a report by the Indian Express newspaper in late September said Kumar's two deputies raised several concerns internally about voter list revisions, registration procedures and digital systems.
At least seven Indian states will hold elections next year, including BJP-ruled Uttar Pradesh, the most populous and considered a bellwether state in national politics.
Verification in Uttar Pradesh began in October 2025 and resulted in 13 per cent of names deleted, according to local media reports.
Voters with their names missing need to prove their credentials before being enrolled, and many have complained about the process.
India started verification of its voter rolls last year ahead of elections in the eastern state of Bihar, ruled by a BJP coalition. The review has now covered the majority of Indian states.

While voter roll revisions are routine, this round became controversial after large numbers of voters in states such as Bihar and West Bengal found their names missing from electoral rolls and were unable to cast ballots.
The BJP won power in West Bengal for the first time in May.

Citing Election Commission data, the BJP says that of the 130 million names deleted from voter lists, 28 million are dead, 63 million have relocated, 10 million are duplicates and 30 million could not be traced by officials.
Opposition parties including Congress have accused Kumar of bias and alleged that the process benefits the BJP.
The Indian Express story said the two deputies to the election commissioner had expressed concerns to Kumar at least 14 times in 10 months but those concerns were not taken into consideration.

The report prompted opposition leaders and members of the youth-led Cockroach Janta Party, which in July forced the education minister to quit after weeks of protest, to launch nationwide demonstrations.

The Election Commission says names are only removed when a voter has died, is mentioned more than once on the rolls, has moved to another region or is untraceable. Officers are required to record detailed reasons why a voter is deleted.
People whose names do not appear in draft rolls can request inclusion before final voter lists are published and also raise appeals if such requests are denied.
Voters excluded from final rolls can also challenge the decision.
To participate in future elections, excluded voters must succeed in their appeals or apply for fresh registration.
Opposition parties argue that arbitrary deletions and lengthy appeals prevented millions in Bihar and West Bengal from voting and could be used as a weapon in future elections.

Kumar has had a difficult relationship with opposition parties since taking over as the election body chief in February 2025. Opposition lawmakers put forward a motion to have him removed earlier this year but it was rejected by parliament.
A 2023 law passed by Modi's government grants the election commission chief immunity from prosecution for acts done in an official capacity.
* The writers are from Reuters

b810470455ad5fad: KUALA LUMPUR: The RM15 billion investment to strengthen the national grid, highlighted in 2027 Budget, will enhance the capacity of the country's electricity supply system to meet growing demand.
In a statement today, Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) said the allocation is part of its RM43 billion investment for the 2025-2027 period to strengthen and modernise the National Grid.
The upgrades will also support the growth of the digital economy and artificial intelligence, which require a stable electricity supply, including for the operation of large-scale data centres.
"Through initiatives such as the Green Lane Pathway, TNB supports efforts to streamline and expedite the development of electricity supply infrastructure for data centre projects," it said.
TNB said the Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme and Green Electricity Tariff also provide industries with options to meet their renewable energy requirements.

For domestic consumers, the utility company welcomed the extension of the electricity bill protection threshold from monthly consumption of 600 kilowatt-hours (kWh) to 800 kWh until Dec 31 this year, as announced on Sept 17.
TNB said the measure is expected to benefit more than eight million domestic consumers, or up to 90 per cent of all domestic consumers.

The company also supported the installation of solar-powered streetlights in villages and rooftop solar panels at welfare homes and places of worship, as well as improvements to electricity supply at tahfiz schools, pondok (religious schools) and Orang Asli villages.
TNB also pledged to heed the government's call to expedite rural electricity supply projects to expand community access to a better electricity supply.

In efforts to empower the Bumiputera economy, TNB said more than RM11 billion has been channelled under the Bumiputera Vendor Development Programme 3.0 (PV 3.0) as of June, benefiting more than 1,200 vendors.

In line with the Bumiputera Economic Transformation Plan 2035, TNB will continue to support the participation of Bumiputera companies in renewable energy projects, grid strengthening and green technology.

TNB also reaffirmed its commitment to implementing the National Energy Transition Roadmap to achieve the net-zero carbon emissions target as well as the aspiration to achieve 70 per cent renewable energy generation capacity by 2050.
These efforts include investments in large-scale solar initiatives, battery energy storage systems and the Hydro Life Extension Programme.
At the regional level, TNB will continue to play its role in the Asean Power Grid project, which has the potential to expand cross-border energy sharing and strengthen energy supply security.

Meanwhile, TNB president and chief executive officer Datuk Seri Shamsul Ahmad said the company's priority is to ensure every household enjoys a safe and reliable electricity supply, while providing businesses with the energy they need to grow.

"As the national electricity utility provider, TNB accepts this responsibility with the utmost integrity. We will continue to work closely with the government and stakeholders to ensure that the development of the country's energy system benefits the people, supports economic growth and leaves a more sustainable future for generations to come," he said.
655b236f36130dc1: KUALA LUMPUR: The RM730 million allocation for sports under the 2027 Budget is a welcome boost, but how much of it will help Malaysia produce their first Olympic champion?

A closer look at the breakdown suggests that much of the immediate focus will be on hosting the SEA Games and Asean Para Games next year, with Malaysia expected to make a strong push for the overall title.
Winning the SEA Games and producing an Olympic champion are two different objectives.
Let's be frank.
Malaysia are expected to finish top of the SEA Games medal table next year.
But will that bring the country any closer to their first Olympic gold medal at the 2028 Los Angeles Games?
Of the total allocation, RM460 million is for national sports development, RM240 million to host the SEA Games and Asean Para Games, and RM30 million for the sports matching grant.

According to the National Sports Council, the RM460 million will support high-performance initiatives, the Road to Gold (RTG) programme, para and deaf athletes, as well as the maintenance of sports facilities nationwide.
The sports allocation is substantial, but winning the SEA Games should not be the main goal.
Malaysia must invest in producing Olympic champions.
With Malaysia hosting the SEA Games next year, featuring 43 sports, the temptation to measure success by the final medal table will be difficult to resist.

Winning the overall title would provide a feel-good factor and give Malaysian athletes and fans plenty to celebrate. Yet it would mean little if the country continued to struggle to produce champions capable of winning at the Olympics.
The SEA Games have their limitations as a measure of a nation's strength in sports.
Host countries have considerable influence over the programme, choosing sports and events that can improve their medal prospects.

While some sports are essential to the regional competition, hosts can also introduce "unusual sports" that offer opportunities to collect gold medals without necessarily advancing their long-term ambitions in Olympic disciplines.
Cambodia provided an example at the 2023 SEA Games when the then-hosts included their traditional martial art, Kun Bokator, in the programme. The hosts won eight gold medals in the sport.

Other editions have featured sports such as fin swimming, underwater hockey and shuttlecock kicking, adding to the medal count but offering limited value to the competing countries' Olympic ambitions.
There is nothing wrong with promoting traditional or non-Olympic sports. They offer athletes opportunities to take on regional rivals and help preserve friendships in sports.
It becomes a problem when collecting medals takes priority instead of developing athletes capable of competing at the highest level.
The SEA Games can be a valuable stepping stone for up-and-coming athletes, while established ones can use them to maintain fitness and boost their ego.
But the overall standings should never be treated as the main measure of a country's strength or Olympic readiness.
The 2028 Los Angeles Olympics are less than two years away, yet identifying and preparing genuine gold-medal prospects remains a challenge.
The RTG is a step in the right direction, but Malaysia must also invest in the next generation of athletes.
What happens when the current generation retires?
The national sports associations (NSAs) cannot keep relying on the same group of elite athletes to deliver results.
Athletes are not robots that can keep producing medals.

A strong sporting system needs a steady supply of quality replacements, with talented youngsters identified early and given the coaching, facilities, sports science and international exposure required to develop.
Too often, attention and resources are given to elite athletes, while the next generation are given limited opportunities to find a clear road to the top.
Malaysia must also be realistic about their Olympic ambitions.
Winning an Olympic gold medal at LA 2028 would be historic, but Malaysia cannot build their strategy around a handful of established names and hope for the best.

The government and NSAs must identify promising athletes early, assess their potential honestly and give them sustained support rather than scrambling for replacements when established stars begin to fade.
The 2027 Budget should be judged not only by Malaysia's SEA Games medal haul, but also by whether it creates a pipeline of athletes capable of challenging the world's best.
Field elite athletes if it serves their preparations, but give promising youngsters opportunities, too.
Some may not win gold next year, but they could become Asian Games medallists and Olympic champions of the future.
Next year's SEA Games, like the previous editions, will see lopsided encounters.
Just imagine Asian Games champions S. Sivasangari and Ng Eain Yow competing for squash gold at next year's SEA Games. Both could wear a pirate's eye patch and still walk away with gold medals.
Malaysia can celebrate being SEA Games champions, and there is nothing wrong with taking pride at home.
But a public holiday and a place at the top of the SEA Games medal table will not automatically make the country a sporting powerhouse.
A country can win more than 100 gold medals at the SEA Games and still struggle to produce Olympic champions.
Malaysia are one fine example.
Malaysia won 111 gold medals when they hosted the SEA Games in 2001. And in 2017, Malaysia took a record of 145 golds as hosts.
Definitely great achievements, but we can label them as "syok sendiri", considering those feats failed to boost Malaysia chances of winning an Olympic title.
That is why Malaysia must take their cue from United States swimmer Michael Phelps, who won 28 Olympic medals, including 23 gold, more Olympic gold medals than most countries have won in total.
Phelps has spoken about the sacrifices required to become the best: "If you want to be the best, you have to do things that other people aren't willing to do."
They are part of a career built on competing against the best in the world, not simply dominating a regional field.
But Malaysia's dream appears to be winning the SEA Games overall title next year while losing sight of their Olympic objective.
That is the test of 2027 Budget.
Whether it helps Malaysia chase more medals at home or build a sporting system capable of producing Olympic champions.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd
d8056910b5fd4616: KUALA LUMPUR: A variety of dishes, cultural experiences and tourism attractions were showcased at the Malaysia Food & Tourism Fair 2026 in Berne, Switzerland, recently, in conjunction with Visit Malaysia Year 2026-2027.

The Embassy of Malaysia in Berne said in a statement to Bernama that more than 450 visitors attended the programme, held on Oct 3 at Mattenhofsaal Hall, to celebrate the country's unique culture, heritage and culinary diversity.
Attendees included local residents, members of the international community and Malaysians living in Switzerland.

"Visitors also had the opportunity to learn more about Malaysia through cultural performances and activities, as well as obtain information on various tourist destinations and attractions across the country," the statement said.

The embassy said the programme not only brought Malaysian flavours and culture closer to the Swiss public but also provided a platform to strengthen ties among the Malaysian community, local residents and friends of Malaysia.
The programme was organised by the Embassy of Malaysia in Berne in collaboration with Tourism Malaysia Frankfurt.
7dd6dda5f5ee52bb: PETALING JAYA: DAP leaders in Negeri Sembilan must continue serving residents even if they no longer hold public office, says party secretary-general Loke Siew Fook.
Loke said former local councillors and village community management council (MPKK) members should continue helping residents who approach them for assistance.

"If voters come for help, please do everything that you can to assist them. Don't say that now that I am no longer in the (state) government or local councils, I can't help," he said in his speech at the Negeri Sembilan DAP convention in Seremban.
"That is not the right way. If people still seek our help even though we are no longer in the state government, it shows they still have confidence in DAP and Pakatan Harapan."
Loke also urged DAP MPs and assemblymen in the state to support grassroots leaders in serving the public.
“Although we no longer have state allocations, that does not mean we can't do anything.
"We used to be in the opposition for decades, and we did not receive allocations. Yet, we found ways to continue our services to the people.”
DAP currently holds nine seats in the state assembly, down from the 11 it won in the 2023 state election. The party lost Chennah and Repah to MCA in the August election.
Loke, who stepped down as Negeri Sembilan DAP chairman after losing Chennah, also said he would not defend his seat on the state committee when the chapter holds its leadership elections next year.
He said he wanted to make way for fresh faces to lead the state chapter and needed to focus on leading the party at the national level.

Loke also reflected on Negeri Sembilan DAP’s growth over the past 22 years, from winning just two state seats in the 2004 general election to securing parliamentary and state seats in subsequent elections and taking over the state government in 2018.
He said he was glad to have led the state chapter for 22 years and supported the need to pass the baton to new leaders.

"Despite being a new state chief, (J Arul Kumar) has a wealth of experience, having worked with me for 10 years. I am confident that under Arul's leadership, Negeri Sembilan DAP will move forward and continue to excel.”
Loke also urged Negeri Sembilan DAP to prepare for all eventualities amid political uncertainty in the state, where menteri besar Ismail Lasim currently has no executive councillors to assist him.
"We need to prepare for any possibility, which includes a (state) election. We don't know that (will happen). But this is something we need to be prepared for.
"Our focus should not be problems facing our opponents … our focus should be on strengthening our party," he said.
73af8b26d2b67c5f: Club issues brief statement about Lachie Cowan and Will Hayward, saying latter suffered minor cut to head after a fall Carlton football club has said two of its players, Lachie Cowan and Will Hayward, required treatment in hospital on Sunday morning in “separate circumstances”. e7b3a26162cc1b65: LONDON: Thousands of people on Saturday joined pro-Palestinian marches in London, Berlin and Dublin calling for an end to Israeli strikes on Gaza, three years after Hamas's Oct 7 attack.
Several thousand marchers in London carried placards reading "End the genocide" and "Free Palestine" as they made their way along the route near the British parliament.
"We are here today to mark three years of the ongoing genocide in Gaza," Aimee Shalan, director of the Palestine Solidarity Campaign, told AFP.
Western sanctions over settler violence did not go far enough, she said, calling for "full sanctions on Israel."
A ceasefire began a year ago and although Israel has reduced its level of attacks it has kept striking Gaza on a near-daily basis.
Strikes have killed some 1,450 Palestinians since the ceasefire, according to Gaza's health ministry.
London police said they had arrested 20 people including a man and a woman with placards supporting the organisation Palestine Action, banned under UK law.
Recent graduate Hibo Hassan, 23, said she was there to show her solidarity.
"Although it is happening in the Middle East, it affects us here now," she said.
"It's extremely dystopian and that is something we should be all scared about," she added.
Another protester, a 32-year-old Kosovar immigrant who gave his name as Kobe, said his own experience of war made him want to "stand up today and not let history repeat" itself.
A small counter-demonstration was organised by Stop The Hate UK, a Jewish-led, pro-Israel campaign group.

Ahead of the protest, organised by the Palestine Coalition, London's Metropolitan Police said it would be using powers under public order legislation to require anyone wearing a face covering to hide their identity to remove it.
"We will take a zero-tolerance approach to hate crime and other offending," said senior Met officer Carl Galvin.
In Berlin, a similar march organised by the group United for Palestine drew around 3,500 people as it set off from a square between the chancellery and parliament, said police.
Many denounced Germany's arms exports to Israel, carrying banners and placards condemning Berlin's military support.
For decades, Germany has seen resolute support for Israel as a fundamental duty largely because of Nazi Germany's responsibility for the genocide of millions of European Jews during the Holocaust.
"I find it really terrible that Germany finds it so difficult to criticise Israel," a student told AFP, who asked not to be named.
In Dublin, protesters took part in a march organised by the Irish Palestine Solidarity Campaign.
Saturday's protests came three days after the third anniversary of the Oct 7, 2023 attack.
The attack was the deadliest in Israel's history, resulting in the deaths of 1,221 people, according to an AFP tally based on official Israeli figures.
Resistance fighters also took 251 hostages into Gaza, 44 of them already dead.
In response, Israel launched a military offensive that has left most of Gaza in ruins and killed more than 74,200 people, according to Gaza's health ministry.

2d40e25dbc411ef0: JAKARTA: Eight orangutans rescued in recent weeks from blazes that tore through Borneo island have been released into a protected forest, Indonesian authorities and rescuers said on Sunday.

The apes were saved from several locations razed by fires -- mostly plantations near their forest homes -- in the West Kalimantan province on the Indonesian side of Borneo last month, the forestry ministry and the YIARI wildlife rehabilitation foundation said in a statement.

The orangutans, three mom and baby pairs as well as two male teenagers, were relocated on Friday to the Batu Nyambu Protected Forest in West Kalimantan, a 23,000-hectare reserve with primary and secondary forest cover.
YIARI CEO Karmele Llano Sanchez said relocating the animals to a new location was a "necessary step" when their habitat was no longer safe.

"Protection of habitats will always be a top priority to ensure orangutans continue to have safe forests to live in, but as long as their habitat remains threatened, rescue is one of the best options we can take to help them survive," Sanchez said.
The reserve was chosen due to availability of food and water sources as well as its connectivity to other forests, said YIARI operational director Argitoe Ranting.
"We want to ensure that rescued orangutans are not simply moved from one place to another, but actually have a chance to survive in their natural habitat," Argitoe said.
Indonesian authorities and YIARI rescued 46 orangutans from threats of fires between August and October 9, local natural resources agency head Murlan Dameria Pane said.
Orangutans are critically endangered, and around 104,000 orangutans remain in Borneo and Sumatra, down from more than 230,000 a century ago, according to conservation group WWF.
Last month, the International Union for Conservation of Nature warned fires were burning in habitats containing 52 percent of Borneo's orangutan population.

Indonesia regularly battles wildfires during the dry season, but the fires have intensified this year because of the El Nino weather phenomenon, set to be one of the strongest since comparable records began four decades ago.
Experts have also pointed to slash-and-burn land-clearing practices that have changed the naturally fire-resistant landscape.
The fires have created severe haze locally, with tens of thousands of cases of respiratory illnesses, and also caused regional air pollution spikes in Singapore and Malaysia.

edb29441bf38c600: Visakhapatnam, INDIA: Handcuffs encircle Google's logo on one campaign poster, while another warns that people "cannot drink data", as opposition mounts to the tech giant's planned artificial intelligence (AI) mega-facility in India.
Excavators have swung into action, clearing forest and farmland on the south-east coast for the US$15 billion construction of Google's largest data centre outside the US.
The project at Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh state, a port often called Vizag, is championed by India as a cornerstone of its technological ambitions.
But many residents fear the data centre -- one of several huge new tech sites in Vizag -- will strain water and power resources, damage the environment and bring too few jobs in return.
Farmer Chandala Sadamma told AFP that when she sees the red-earth scars where her plot of mango and cashew trees once stood, "I feel like crying".
She was paid more than US$82,000 for the two-acre (0.80-hectare) stretch of land, but the transaction left a bitter taste.
"Some company came and, without showing any respect, they took the land and we accepted it," the 50-year-old said.
Vizag is a landing point for submarine internet cables linking the country to Singapore, so for India, the location of the 600-acre site -- more than 340 football pitches -- is ideal.
The "AI Hub investment is a multi-decade commitment" carrying "an obligation to be a good neighbour", said Alexander Smith, Google's head of infrastructure and energy for Asia-Pacific.
"The watershed, the grid and the communities around our facilities must be better off for our being here."
The Andhra Pradesh government told AFP that in addition to financial compensation, new housing is being built and handed over to people who had lived on the site.
'WHY HERE?'
Governments and tech firms worldwide are spending trillions of dollars on data centres -- boxy buildings stuffed with racks of computer servers that power apps and AI tools.
But the developments have sparked backlash in many countries, with a Finnish authority recently ordering work to halt on two Google data centre sites pending mandatory environmental assessments.
Activists in Andhra Pradesh are also demanding a moratorium on new data centres across the state until independent environmental and social impact evaluations are published.
"The United States has a huge coast... They can simply set it up there," Gutta Rohith of the local campaign group Human Rights Forum told AFP at a meeting of around 150 people.
"Why are they coming here?"
Opposition to data centres, including in the US, often takes aim at the use of local water resources to cool hot servers down.
Google said it will use "advanced" air cooling technology instead at the India hub, while the state plans six 1.20-gigawatt nuclear power plants as energy demand soars.
Still, water use worries residents, especially given plans for Vizag to become a tech megahub.
"They are saying that Google is being established for the education and employment opportunities of our children," said shopkeeper Gubbala Ramanamma.
But "we are already struggling with water scarcity", the 57-year-old said, standing beside a dry well.
LAND PRICES

Google said its data centre will generate US$688 million in local economic activity each year and support about 4,200 jobs during construction, with hundreds of specialist jobs once operational in 2028.
Andhra Pradesh's government also said it expects "188,000 direct and indirect jobs to be generated".
But Rohith said the economic benefits would not necessarily trickle down from the warehouse-like facilities.
"We need mass employment and labour-intensive industries, not high-capital industries."
Google is not alone -- a joint venture between Reliance Industries, Brookfield and Digital Realty is investing US$11 billion in another AI data centre in Vizag.

Land prices have risen by an average of "more than 45 per cent" since the city unveiled its development plans, said E. Ashok Kumar, Visakhapatnam head of the Confederation of Real Estate Developers' Associations of India.
Meanwhile, as AI use accelerates, the world's most populous nation has rolled out incentives to attract big tech companies, including tax cuts.
Despite its widespread internet and app use generating nearly a fifth of the world's digital data, India has only about three per cent of global data centre capacity, government figures show.

Andhra Pradesh Technology Minister Nara Lokesh, in an interview with AFP in February, spoke of investment agreements worth US$175 billion involving 760 projects -- and vowed to "execute these projects at a pace that the country has never seen".
Lokesh has also insisted that "residential requirements will always be prioritised over data centres", according to a statement.
"The water needs of our people will always come first."
Visakhapatnam environmental campaigner EAS Sarma, a former senior government official who worked in the power and finance ministries, has called for a water audit by an independent agency.
"Civilisations have vanished because of water shortages," he warned.

f4ac19bf34ba6be2: KUALA LUMPUR: The 2027 Budget's personal tax relief measures are expected to provide additional financial breathing room for middle-income earners (M40), while targeted incentives for businesses and investors could support investment growth, according to PwC Malaysia.
Its tax partner Michelle Chuo said the increase in personal tax relief from RM9,000 to RM12,000, the first adjustment since 2010, was timely amid continued cost-of-living pressures.
She said the higher relief, together with the one-percentage-point reduction in income tax rates for the M40, would provide additional disposable income for taxpayers in the group.

"Against the backdrop of continued cost of living pressures, the personal tax measures announced in 2027 Budget are a welcome move, particularly for the M40," she told Bernama in response to the 2027 Budget tabled by Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on Friday.
The budget proposed a one-percentage-point reduction in tax rates for chargeable income between RM70,000 and RM150,000.
However, for high-income earners, the budget proposed raising the tax rate for chargeable income exceeding RM1 million to 30 per cent from the current 28 per cent.

Chuo said the higher personal relief would benefit taxpayers more broadly, but the savings for higher-income earners could be partly offset by the higher top marginal tax rate and the lower threshold at which it applies.
"For higher-income earners, the additional tax at the top end will progressively offset the savings from the higher relief and lower tax rates.
"This suggests a deliberate policy tilt towards directing more of the net tax benefits to middle-income taxpayers, while preserving the progressivity of the tax system," she said.

On the corporate front, PwC Malaysia tax partner and private leader Fung Mei Lin said enhancements to the Global Services Hub incentive would strengthen Malaysia's appeal as a regional base for multinational companies.

She said extending the scheme to treasury and fund activities, alongside withholding tax relief on interest and stamp duty exemptions for intercompany loan agreements, would provide stronger incentives for multinationals to establish regional treasury and financing functions in Malaysia, including under the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) package.
"Together with the expatriate spouse working rights and the Malaysian Asean Business Entity (MyABE) initiative, it forms a coherent 'invest, hire and grow here' package," she said.

Fung also welcomed the extension of income tax exemptions for individual investors through equity crowdfunding (ECF) platforms and angel investors financing early-stage technology startups until end-2030.

She said the RM270 million allocation for small and medium enterprises, mid-tier companies and social enterprises through ECF and peer-to-peer (P2P) financing platforms would further support the startup financing ecosystem and help deepen the funding pipeline.

On green investments, Fung said the continued commitment to supporting the low-carbon transition, coupled with a more clearly defined scope of qualifying expenditure, could help channel incentives towards investments with greater impact.

Meanwhile, she said the one-percentage-point reduction in the income tax rate for micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), alongside a higher capital allowance threshold for businesses, would ease their cash-flow pressures.

Nonetheless, she said as the budget measures are legislated, businesses will welcome clear and practical guidance, including on how the incentives interact with global minimum tax rules, so that the benefits intended for investors are fully realised.

Fung also called for careful consideration of the Reinvestment Allowance review, which has supported manufacturers and other businesses investing in Malaysia for decades, saying a more targeted design should preserve industrial competitiveness while providing clear eligibility criteria and transitional arrangements.
"As the review progresses, we would encourage early engagement with the industry on the eligibility criteria and how the incentive is delivered," she said.

Fung welcomed the introduction of a Multi-Family Office (MFO) model in Forest City alongside the existing Single Family Office (SFO) scheme, saying it could broaden Malaysia's wealth management industry, attract families with different asset sizes and create demand for local fund managers, trustees, accountants and legal professionals.

She said clear guidance on licensing, tax treatment, substance requirements, and how the MFO and SFO schemes interact would be important to attract participants and establish Malaysia as a trusted wealth management centre.

Overall, she said 2027 Budget demonstrated that fiscal discipline and growth support could complement each other, but timely legislation and clear implementation guidance would be crucial to translating policy incentives into tangible outcomes.
"Certainty is what turns incentives into reality," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd
81a2d82df0771121: PETALING JAYA: Universiti Teknologi Malaysia (UTM) perlu mempertimbangkan semula keputusan memecat seorang profesor madya selepas Mahkamah Tinggi Johor Bahru memutuskan bahawa proses tatatertib universiti itu telah menafikan peluang yang adil kepadanya untuk membela diri.

“Hak untuk didengar mestilah hak yang sebenar dan bukannya sekadar formaliti kosong,” katanya, merujuk kepada prinsip undang-undang yang mantap dalam prosiding semakan kehakiman.

Malarvili, yang berkhidmat di kampus UTM Skudai, Johor selama kira-kira 21 tahun, berdepan dakwaan berkaitan penggunaan tandatangan yang diimbas pada surat sokongan, perjalanan ke luar negara tanpa kelulusan, ketidakaturan rekod kehadiran, aktiviti berkaitan program UNISERF serta dakwaan penglibatan dalam aktiviti perniagaan luar.
UTM dan kedua-dua jawatankuasa tatatertib diperintahkan membayar kos sebanyak RM15,000 kepada Malarvili secara bersama dan berasingan.
Ebrina Zubir mewakili Malarvili, manakala Syahmi Nawawi mewakili UTM dan kedua-dua jawatankuasa berkenaan.

c22b2f3183aeee9f: NEW YORK, Oct 11 — New York’s subway is known for being dirty, noisy and sometimes flooded, but that doesn’t stop people from flocking to grab a seat, sign or other memorabilia at a unique annual auction.
In south Brooklyn, shoppers hoping to get a slice of the city’s transit service waited for hours to trawl through an open-air market organised by city authorities.
Each person gets a maximum of 45 minutes to search, allowing others to come in after them.
Nori Juba, 61, found what he was looking for: a large sign bearing the name of Grand Central station, along with the numbers of the subway lines he takes every day.
The train system is “old and creaky and it’s outdated”, he admitted.

“But I think that’s what makes it interesting. And this piece of metal is dirty. It smells like a subway station, but there’s something about it that makes it real New York, one of a kind in the world.”
The prices aren’t cheap: a medium-sized sign cost around US$500, while larger ones can run past US$1,000.
The iconic orange plastic seats from the New York subway go for around US$900 each.

The NYC Transit’s annual pop-up sale in New York. — AFP pic
Celebrities are sometimes spotted at the market, and this month New York resident and filmmaker Spike Lee was stopping for pictures with fellow shoppers.
He proudly showed off the metal sign he just bought, marked “Penn Station”, the subway stop for Madison Square Garden — the arena where his beloved Knicks basketball team plays.
“I don’t take the subway anymore to the big games,” he confessed to reporters, but recalled riding the train regularly while growing up — noting he always paid his fare.
“I never jumped the turnstile either. Let the record state!” he joked.
‘A piece of New York’
New York’s Metropolitan Transportation Authority has always resold its signs to collectors but more recently opened up sales to the public, said Paul Dvoskin, the director in charge of the programme.

fb94a32089ccbee7: PETALING JAYA: Universiti Teknologi Malaysia (UTM) must reconsider its dismissal of an associate professor after the High Court in Johor Bahru ruled that the disciplinary process had denied her a fair opportunity to defend herself.

Judicial Commissioner Budiman Lutfi Mohamed set aside the disciplinary committee’s decision on Nov 29, 2024, which upheld eight charges against associate professor B Malarvili and maintained her dismissal, effective June 4 that year.

He ordered UTM to review the case afresh, disclose relevant evidence, allow Malarvili to make further representations and consider whether witnesses should be heard or further investigations carried out.
However, the ruling does not amount to a finding that Malarvili was innocent of the charges, as the court did not order UTM to reinstate her or pay salary arrears or damages.

In his written judgment, Budiman said the fresh review could result in the charges being withdrawn, Malarvili being cleared, a lesser punishment being imposed or her dismissal being upheld again, provided the process complied with the law.

He said that the case was not simply about whether the disciplinary committee had reached the correct conclusion, but whether Malarvili had been given a meaningful opportunity to answer the allegations.
“The right to be heard must be a real right and not an empty formality,” he said, referring to an established legal principle in judicial review proceedings.
Budiman said admitting to using a scanned signature did not necessarily amount to admitting to forgery, dishonesty or an intention to deceive.

The judge also found that UTM had not shown that the requested documents had been provided or adequately explained how Malarvili’s representations were considered after the disciplinary appeal committee referred the case back for reconsideration.

Malarvili, who had served at UTM’s Skudai campus in Johor for about 21 years, faced allegations involving the use of a scanned signature on a supporting letter, overseas travel without approval, attendance-record irregularities, activities linked to the UNISERF programme and alleged involvement in outside business activities.
UTM and the two disciplinary committees were ordered to pay Malarvili RM15,000 in costs, jointly and severally.
Ebrina Zubir appeared for Malarvili, while Syahmi Nawawi represented UTM and the two committees.
61fc5887a4f92c92: LETTER: Malaysia's 2027 Budget, with a total allocation of RM510 billion, sets out a comprehensive plan to support economic growth while addressing the needs of the people.
The increase from RM470 billion in the previous year signals the government's continued efforts to strengthen public services, support households and invest in the country's future.
The RM16 billion allocation for Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) is an important measure to help households manage rising living costs.
For many lower- and middle-income households, such assistance can provide much-needed relief, particularly in meeting daily expenses such as food and other basic necessities.
However, the longer-term benefit should go beyond easing immediate financial pressures. The assistance should also contribute to greater household financial resilience.
From a broader economic perspective, assistance to households also supports domestic consumption.
When families spend on essential goods and services, local retailers, small businesses and suppliers may benefit from the additional demand.
Another important aspect of the budget is the investment in human capital.
The government has allocated RM8 billion for Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET), alongside RM3 billion through HRD Corp to provide three million training opportunities.

These allocations reflect the government's efforts to prepare the workforce for changes in the labour market, particularly with the growing importance of artificial intelligence, automation and digital technologies.
However, the real economic value of these programmes will be reflected in what happens after the workforce training.
Are they able to secure better jobs? Do their new skills lead to higher wages? Are employers benefiting from improved productivity?

A more skilled workforce can help businesses adopt new technologies, improve efficiency and remain competitive. Over time, productivity improvements can also create greater opportunities for wage growth.

The budget's RM57 billion financing and guarantee facilities supporting micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and strategic sectors will help smaller businesses, particularly those looking to expand operations, invest in equipment or adopt new technologies.
The broader benefits emerge when businesses use these facilities to expand production, increase sales and create employment opportunities.

For example, a small food manufacturer that obtains financing to purchase new equipment may be able to increase production capacity leading to greater demand for raw materials, additional workers and more business for local suppliers.

Beyond individual programmes, the 2027 Budget also reflects the government's commitment to fiscal consolidation, with the fiscal deficit targeted to decline to 3.3 per cent of gross domestic product (GDP).
This is an important step towards maintaining fiscal sustainability while continuing to support economic development and public welfare.
Managing public finances responsibly is not only about controlling expenditure but also about ensuring that available resources are used effectively and deliver value to the economy and society.
Overall, next year's budget presents a positive direction for Malaysia's economic development by addressing both immediate household needs and longer-term growth priorities.
Financial assistance helps support household consumption, while investments in skills and business financing can strengthen the country's productive capacity.

These measures complement one another. Supporting household spending helps sustain domestic demand, while improving skills and business capabilities enables the economy to produce more efficiently and create better employment opportunities.
The next step is to ensure that the programmes are implemented effectively and that their outcomes are consistently monitored.

The significance of 2027 Budget goes beyond its RM510 billion allocation. Its real value lies in how these resources can improve household financial security, raise productivity, create quality jobs and strengthen Malaysia's economic resilience.
ASSOC PROFESSOR DR RASIDAH MOHD RASHID
Research Fellow

70818bd513065891: KUALA LUMPUR: The increase in the Rubber Production Incentive (IPG) to RM3.30 per kilogramme (kg) in the tabling of 2027 Budget is expected to help cover part of production costs and provide additional income support for smallholders.

927ec5c935956ad7: SINGAPORE, Oct 11 — Travelling overseas, especially to a destination like Singapore, certainly isn’t budget friendly.
But that didn’t stop a 16-year-old Thai teenager from taking his grandfather on his first trip to the little red dot.
“As a 16-year-old boy, not from a wealthy family, I took my grandfather on a train journey covering 2,000km to Singapore for the first time,” he wrote in an Instagram post on Tuesday (Oct 6).
In a series of accompanying posts, the teenager, who goes by kollawat_2626, or Queue, documented the journey from Thailand to Singapore, travelling by train, bus and on foot.
Queue and his grandfather’s 2,000km journey to Singapore involved taking trains, buses and walking on foot. PHOTO: Instagram/kollawat_2626
They started from Nakhon Pathom province to Su-ngai Kolok district in Narathiwat province, before crossing the border into Malaysia.
According to Queue, they had taken a third-class train, described as the cheapest class.
The pair then took a bus to Pasir Mas railway station in Kelantan.
From there, they spent around 390 baht ($14.80) per person for a train towards Johor Bahru and crossed the Causeway into Singapore by bus, which cost 50 baht each.
“I travelled by train from Kanchanaburi to Singapore without taking a plane. At 16, I actually managed to do it. All that exhaustion just disappeared,” said Queue.
While it was his grandfather’s first time here, the teenager was no stranger to Singapore.
He had previously visited in 2022, during which he visited the Merlion Park.
During their recent trip, he once again visited the iconic attraction, this time taking photographs with his grandfather.
And despite Singapore being their main destination, the pair reportedly chose to stay overnight in Johor Bahru to save costs, where they spent 2,000 baht a night, according to Queue.
He also shared that a man he regarded as an older brother had helped cover their accommodation expenses.
The 16-year-old’s journey has since drawn an outpouring of support from netizens, with his most popular Instagram post garnering over 792,000 likes and 4,000 comments.
“You are so lucky to have had the opportunity to take your grandfather on a trip,” said a commenter.

Another wrote: “You did an amazing job. Even when I travelled alone with everything prepared, I was still nervous. But you’re only 16 and you brought your grandfather along too. That’s something to be proud of.” — AsiaOne
412f927b4cef13cd: BANGKOK: Finance officials from around the world will gather in Thailand this week under the shadow of a widening war in the Middle East, the biggest energy supply shock ever and rising interest rates that together pose daunting risks to already sluggish global economic growth.

The US-Israeli-led war with Iran, now in its eighth month, and the inflation and hardship it has caused, will dominate the agenda and sideline conversations during the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank, being held outside Washington for the first time in three years.
Notably absent will be US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who dispatched two senior officials in his stead while he handled some "domestic engagements", a US official said.

His decision to skip the high-profile gathering and a meeting of the Group of 20 major economies, which the US leads this year, may frustrate counterparts amid rising tensions over the Iran war, Ukraine's battle against Russia's invasion and the US move to impose sanctions on the International Criminal Court.

World Bank President Ajay Banga told Reuters that while global growth had held up better than feared when Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz, shutting off some 20 per cent of the world's oil, pressures were building again.
Soaring diesel prices, rising fertiliser prices and a looming "super" El Nino weather effect that experts say could lead to 450,000 heat-related deaths are all hitting at once.

Group of Seven countries have agreed to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude oil from emergency reserves under pressure from US President Donald Trump, who is keen to see lower petrol prices before November elections that could see his Republican Party lose control of Congress.

Trump on Friday announced a deal with Russia that would provide even more diesel to global markets and a temporary waiver of US sanctions designed to deprive Moscow of revenues for its war on Ukraine.
The move drew swift criticism from Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy.

More than one billion barrels of oil have been released mainly from onshore commercial inventories since the start of the war on Feb 28, but industry executives say the amount of oil in storage that is accessible to the global market is running low, making the market more fragile and fuelling pressure on prices.
Banga said the Bank was not revising down its global forecasts at the moment, but was keeping a close eye on developments.

"The real thing is not just El Nino by itself; it's the combination ... What's happening to fertiliser prices? What's happening to energy costs? What's happening to debt? It's that put together that creates its own challenges," he said. "And I think that will call upon all of us to be far more careful on what we prepare for in the coming months."
RISING DEBT
IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva issued a similar warning in her traditional curtain-raiser speech previewing the meetings, telling the audience, "Winter is coming."
The IMF has signalled little change in its forecast for three per cent global growth in 2026 and may edge its forecast for next year slightly higher.
But some countries will see downgrades, including Ukraine, now in its fifth year of war against Russia's invasion, and Gulf countries hit by Iranian strikes and sharply reduced energy exports.

IMF research released on Tuesday showed that sharp spikes in food and energy prices are an increasingly common source of crises that drive inflation expectations higher for longer, worsen poverty and threaten economic stability.
One huge headache for policymakers is the growing public debt burden that is sapping growth and adding inflationary pressures.
The IMF says public debt is at the highest level since World War Two and will exceed 100 per cent of GDP before 2030.

Advanced economies, led by the US, have the highest debt-to-GDP ratios, but emerging markets and low-income countries are particularly vulnerable, given a perfect storm of challenges: capital outflows in search of higher US rates, El Nino, and lack of investment in AI, which has mitigated negative supply shocks in the US and other rich countries.
EMERGING MARKET CONCERNS

Developing countries are particularly vulnerable given high public debt levels that will have to be renegotiated at higher interest rates. Interest payments already exceed 10 per cent of revenue in developing countries on average.

Early in the Covid crisis, G20 leaders announced a suspension of debt service payments for the poorest countries, but there is little appetite for such action now, according to diplomats from G20 countries, who said high debt levels and political pressures posed bigger hurdles this time.

Many lower-income countries are worried about new IMF recommendations for loan programmes that call for fewer, but deeper reforms as a condition for approving lending, a change that many fear will lead to painful austerity measures.
"Countries are already cutting their expenditures because their debt payments are going high and because of the IMF conditionality," said Iolanda Fresnillo, who works on debt justice for Eurodad.
"We fear that this review of conditionality policy is just going to make things worse."
Kenya, she said, had avoided a debt restructuring by cutting public expenditures and trying to raise taxes, but the changes sparked significant protests, especially by the young.
The IMF risked losing credibility unless it acknowledged the severity of the crisis facing many developing countries.
"As long as they continue with the governance structure that they have, they are becoming less and less relevant," she said.
SECURITY AND FINANCE

Flight routes to Bangkok often route through the Middle East, posing immediate security challenges to the more than 10,000 travellers descending on Thailand's bustling capital city of nine million residents following recent attacks on Saudi airports.

The last off-site annual meetings of the IMF and World Bank took place in Morocco just days after militants led by Hamas killed 1,200 people in Israel, followed by Israel's bombardment of Gaza that killed more than 74,000 people and devastated cities throughout the Palestinian area.

Three years later, the linkage between national security and international finance is clear, although finance officials at the time had dismissed the Hamas attack as not being an economic issue, said Josh Lipsky, vice president of international economics at the Atlantic Council.

"Obviously there have been massive global ramifications," he said. "What we're currently experiencing with Iran and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz has a direct connection with what happened three years ago."
Policymakers needed to become more agile in responding to geopolitical crises in an increasingly interconnected world, Lipsky said.
"They have to be proactive and they have to recognize that they don't live in the world they used to."

ea560eeb75d3c19c: PETALING JAYA: PAS wajar memperuntukkan satu pertiga kerusi di empat negeri ditadbirnya kepada Umno, jika dua parti itu mahu meneruskan kerjasama dalam pilihan raya akan datang, kata Ahli Majlis Kerja Tertinggi (MKT) Umno, Nur Jazlan Mohamed.
