"Pengundi bukan Melayu praktikal, terutama masyarakat Cina yang melihat jika parti politik boleh memberikan kehidupan dan kesejahteraan lebih baik, mereka akan memilih. Walaupun banyak prejudis yang telah dilekatkan kepada parti macam Umno dan juga parti macam PAS."
f5903678a56f2957: GEORGE TOWN: The Consumers' Association of Penang (CAP) has called for tougher penalties, including lifetime driving bans and mandatory jail terms, for motorists caught driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs.

CAP senior education officer N.V. Subbarow said drink-driving and driving under the influence of drugs posed a serious threat to road users, with innocent pedestrians and motorists paying the price for reckless behaviour.
He called on the Transport Ministry and police to step up enforcement through regular roadblocks, alcohol screening and drug tests on motorists suspected of driving under the influence.
Subbarow said offenders should have their licences revoked immediately. He also called for heavier fines and longer jail terms to deter repeat offences.
"Drink-driving is a preventable crime that puts innocent lives at risk.
"Those who engage in such behaviour must face severe consequences, particularly when their actions result in serious injuries or deaths," he said today.

When tabling the 2027 Budget, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said motorists who caused accidents while driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs would be required to compensate their victims under a proposed amendment to the Road Transport Act.
He said the proposed amendment would make compensation mandatory for victims of accidents involving drunk drivers or motorists high on drugs.
Subbarow said some motorists appeared to regard drinking alcohol or taking drugs before driving as normal, despite the serious danger they posed to other road users.
"We demand stricter measures to prevent alcohol from being carried in vehicles, including motorcycles, to curb drink-driving," he said.
He stressed that enforcement must be firm, consistent and carried out without fear or favour to ensure offenders were held accountable.
Motorists must not be allowed to endanger lives on the road, he said, reiterating his call for lifetime driving bans for those caught driving under the influence.
"Roads must be safe, not places where innocent people live in fear," he added.
2d3b0452674f3e02: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Corruption Watch (MCW) has called for an independent, comprehensive and transparent reinvestigation into allegations that a senior Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) officer received RM350,000, stressing that the probe must be free from conflicts of interest.

MCW president Jais Abdul Karim said the organisation welcomed MACC's formation of a special team to reinvestigate the case, but stressed that its task must go beyond reviewing the old investigation papers.
He said MACC's disclosure that the case was closed in 2018 due to a lack of evidence had raised questions about the credibility of the original investigation.
"This admission raises very important questions. The public has the right to know the actual scope of the investigation conducted in 2018.
"What evidence was examined and, most importantly, what was the basis for closing the case, which now has to be reopened?" he said.

Jais said the special team should also examine the possibility of charges under Section 165 of the Penal Code, rather than limiting its investigation to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2009.
"Section 165 provides for punishment of public servants who obtain valuable items without adequate consideration from individuals connected to their official duties.
"It is a stringent provision that does not require direct proof of corrupt intent," he said.
To ensure that those overseeing the investigation were also held accountable, Jais proposed involving an independent external oversight mechanism in the process.
He said the principle of justice must be upheld and no individual should be convicted through a trial on social media.
"If no wrongdoing is established, the individual's name must be cleared transparently.
"But if there is evidence of criminal misconduct, action must be taken without compromise or protection.
"MACC must uphold the principle of being 'whiter than white' — not only being clean, but also being seen to be clean, independent and with integrity," he said.
Yesterday, MACC formed a special team to investigate and review an old allegation involving the receipt of RM350,000 linked to one of its senior officers.
The case was initially investigated in 2018, but the investigation papers were closed after investigators found that no elements of a corruption offence could be established at the time.

However, MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman ordered the investigation to be reopened following renewed attention to the allegation, which recently went viral and sparked discussion on social media.
d0cec2697ba2386f: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 11 — Putrajaya Corporation and the Federal Territories Department have been asked to review the allocation they are expected to receive under Budget 2027 to strengthen care and improve the welfare of senior citizens, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh.
She said existing approaches must be adapted to the physical and social needs of senior citizens, including those who are bedridden, live alone or have lost their spouses.

Programmes for senior citizens, she said, should not focus solely on physical activities such as aerobics and brisk walking, but should also include activities suited to their abilities and interests.

“The needs of a 60-year-old are very different from those of an 80-year-old. If we do not consider their needs and organise programmes that are convenient for us to run but difficult for them to participate in, we will fail to meet those needs,” she said.
She was speaking at the Putrajaya-level Federal Territories Senior Citizens’ Day celebration here today.
Hannah said loneliness among the elderly also needed attention, as those living alone or who had lost their spouses were at risk of being socially isolated and falling victim to scams.
“Having many children and grandchildren does not mean they are not lonely. In fact, they may feel even lonelier because everyone is busy with their own schedules,” she said.
As such, she proposed that community centres and places of worship reach out to senior citizens who had lost their spouses and organise follow-up activities to ensure they were not left alone.
She said such efforts should be extended to senior citizens who are unable to attend programmes at Senior Citizens’ Activity Centres so that they, too, could receive the social support they needed.
Hannah also pledged her support for the Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development in its efforts to empower vulnerable groups, including senior citizens. — Bernama
0eedd9d29d15f035: WASHINGTON: US consumer sentiment slumped further in early October as the rising cost of living because of the Middle East conflict soured households' views of the economy, more bad news for President Donald Trump ahead of the Nov 3 midterm elections.

The University of Michigan's Surveys of Consumers was the latest in a series of recent polls to capture the darkening mood among Americans, who are being squeezed by high inflation and borrowing costs.
Trump's approval rating is at the lowest of his political career amid angst over his handling of the economy.
Next month's elections will determine control of Congress.
The US-Israeli war has raised energy prices, fanning inflation and prompting the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates in September for the first time in three years.
Sentiment deteriorated sharply this month among lower-income consumers and those with smaller stock portfolios, the University of Michigan said on Friday.

There was also a decline in morale among respondents identifying as Independents. Though there was an uptick among Democrats and Republicans, sentiment remained considerably lower than it was in January this year.
"Consumers across the political spectrum are frustrated with rising prices and a sense of treading water financially," said Jim Baird, chief investment officer at Plante Moran Financial Advisors.
"It may not be readily apparent in headline gross domestic product data, but it's likely to be very apparent as voters cast their ballots in the coming weeks."
The University of Michigan's Consumer Sentiment Index dropped to 46.30 this month from 48.10 in September. The third straight monthly decline pushed sentiment close to a record low plumbed in May.
Economists polled by Reuters had forecast the index at 47.80.
The survey's measure of current economic conditions slumped to an all-time low of 44.70 from 50.90 in September.
Consumers' expectations improved modestly, though buying conditions for durable goods plunged amid high prices and borrowing costs.
HIGHER-INCOME HOUSEHOLDS DRIVING SPENDING
Weak sentiment likely does not mean a significant slowdown in consumer spending as the relationship between the two has weakened over the years.

The economy also resembles what economists describe as a K-shape, where higher-income households are doing well, partly thanks to strong stock market performance, compared with their middle- and lower-income counterparts, whose budgets are under strain.
Consumer spending is mostly being driven by higher-income households.

That was reinforced by a separate report from the University of Michigan showing just under a third of consumers expected to spend as usual in the coming year on items that have experienced large price increases, while 54 per cent said they would cut back.
About 16 per cent of consumers said they would stop buying.
It noted that higher-income consumers were more likely to maintain spending than their lower-income counterparts.
"So, as long as equity markets hold up, spending can keep going," said James Knightley, chief international economist at ING.
"Hopefully, that buys time for an improvement in the energy situation that provides relief in terms of lower motor fuel costs and improved job prospects for the broader household sector."
"But if we were to experience a stock market correction, then the situation would change quickly."

The Surveys of Consumers' measure of consumer expectations for inflation over the next year nudged up to 4.70 per cent from 4.60 per cent in September. Twelve-month inflation expectations have surged from 3.40 per cent in February before the US-Israeli war with Iran started.
Consumers' expectations for inflation over the next five years rose to 3.50 per cent from 3.40 per cent in September.

The US central bank last month raised its overnight benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points to the 3.75 per cent-4.00 per cent range, the first hike in three years, and flagged further increases in borrowing costs in the months ahead.

The odds of another rate hike this month were diminished by the underwhelming payroll gains in September as well as cooler-than-expected inflation readings for July and August. Economists expect the Fed to raise rates in December.

f0da563af23eac62: PETALING JAYA: Integriti dan penguatkuasaan berkesan menjadi kunci membendung penipuan kargo kerana undang-undang semata-mata tidak menjamin barangan dilepaskan mengikut prosedur, kata seorang bekas timbalan pendakwa raya.
Devanandan S Subramaniam berkata kelemahan dalam prosedur pelepasan kastam boleh menyebabkan kargo dilepaskan walaupun dokumen penting berkaitan pemilikan barangan tidak lengkap atau tidak tersedia.
Beliau berkata dokumen seperti borang K1, manifes dan bil muatan perlu disemak sebelum kargo dibenarkan keluar.
Bagaimanapun, beliau mengakui tidak pasti bagaimana prosedur itu dilaksanakan ketika ini dengan penggunaan dokumen elektronik.
“Integriti memainkan peranan. Kita boleh mempunyai semua undang-undang yang diperlukan, tetapi jika pegawai tidak mempunyai integriti, perkara seperti ini masih boleh berlaku,” katanya.

Devanandan, yang pernah mengendalikan kes jenayah komersial di Jabatan Peguam Negara, berkata demikian pada forum Strengthening Malaysia’s Downstream Petroleum Value Chain and Identifying Gaps and Enabling Factors Within Malaysia’s Regulatory Landscape, anjuran Maritime Network Sdn Bhd dengan kerjasama Universiti Malaysia Terengganu (UMT).

Berkongsi pengalaman mengendalikan kes penipuan kargo lebih 20 tahun lalu, beliau berkata antara cabaran utama pendakwaan ialah membuktikan bukan sahaja dokumen dipalsukan, tetapi tertuduh juga mengetahui dokumen itu palsu.
Beliau memberi contoh kes membabitkan kargo bernilai kira-kira USD2 juta yang sepatutnya dihantar ke Chittagong, Bangladesh, tetapi sebaliknya dipunggah di Pelabuhan Klang.

Menurutnya, kargo itu berasal dari Belawan, Sumatera namun pihak penyewa kapal kemudian mengarahkan nakhoda mengubah haluan ke Pelabuhan Klang, sedangkan pihak pengirim masih memegang bil muatan asal sebagai bukti hak milik barangan.
Menurutnya, kargo itu tetap dipunggah selepas ejen pelepasan memperoleh kelulusan diperlukan. Siasatan kemudian menemukan dokumen palsu, termasuk borang kastam K1.
Pengarah urusan syarikat terbabit didakwa menggunakan dokumen palsu sebagai tulen, manakala syarikat itu berdepan pertuduhan menerima harta curi.
Bagaimanapun, kes berkenaan digugurkan kerana pendakwaan gagal membuktikan pengarah urusan itu mengetahui atau mempunyai alasan munasabah untuk mempercayai dokumen berkenaan palsu.
Devanandan berkata kes itu menunjukkan bahawa penemuan dokumen palsu sahaja tidak mencukupi untuk membuktikan kesalahan tertuduh jika pengetahuan mengenai pemalsuan tidak dapat dibuktikan.
Beliau menegaskan pegawai kastam bertanggungjawab memastikan semua dokumen disahkan sebelum kargo dibenarkan meninggalkan pelabuhan atau kawasan di bawah kawalan kastam.

“Selagi mereka memastikan semuanya teratur, perkara seperti ini tidak akan berlaku,” katanya, sambil menambah bahawa penggunaan dokumen elektronik mungkin mengubah proses pemeriksaan, tetapi keberkesanannya tetap bergantung pada integriti pegawai.
4dcd7c5ea6376318: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has strongly condemned the deadly attack on Saudi Arabia’s King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, which killed civilians and injured hundreds.
In a Facebook post today, Anwar said the attack had claimed innocent lives and left hundreds injured, while extending his condolences to the victims’ families and wishing those hurt a swift recovery.
“I unequivocally denounce the attack on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh, which has taken innocent lives and left hundreds injured,” he said.
Anwar said attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure could not be justified, warning that such actions would only deepen the suffering caused by the conflict.
“There can be no justification for attacks against civilians and civilian infrastructure,” he said, adding that putting innocent lives at risk would only worsen the consequences of the conflict.
He also reaffirmed Malaysia’s support for Saudi Arabia and its people amid the situation.
“Malaysia stands in solidarity with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and its people at this perilous hour,” he said.

Anwar expressed hope that diplomatic efforts would prevail before the conflict widened further, saying Malaysia remained steadfast in its hope that “diplomacy and reason will prevail before the conflict widens still further”.
c1ef17739b3d55e9: KUALA LUMPUR: Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail has declined to comment on claims that Rohingya entered Malaysia using Bangladeshi passports before obtaining refugee cards in the country.
He said such claims had to be supported by strong and clear evidence before he could respond, according to Utusan Malaysia.

"If there are strong arguments and clear evidence, only then can I respond. So far, the matter is not within my knowledge," he said after the National Surah al-Hujurat Discourse in Kulim yesterday.
He was asked to comment on claims that Rohingya refugees had entered Malaysia using Bangladeshi passports before registering with the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR).
Recently, a content creator uploaded a video of his visit to Bangladesh featuring a Rohingya man who claimed to have used a Bangladeshi passport to enter and leave Malaysia.

The man claimed in the interview that he had initially been in Malaysia without a valid passport or travel document before obtaining a Bangladeshi passport with the help of the embassy and the Immigration Department.
He also claimed that his parents, who live in Bangladesh, had helped him obtain the document.

In a separate development, Saifuddin left it to the authorities to complete investigations into allegations that Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) director-general Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain had assaulted two policemen.
He said the investigation papers, containing witness statements and other evidence gathered during the investigation, had been submitted to the Attorney-General's Chambers (A-GC).
"At this stage, I have no comment, and I leave it to the relevant parties," he said.
Previously, the A-GC was reported to have returned the investigation papers on the incident involving Shuhaily to the police for further investigation.
Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar was reported to have said that several aspects of the investigation needed further examination before any action could be finalised.
6fe68453680692aa: KASAULI, Oct 11 — Writer Salman Rushdie once described the Himalayas as “land’s attempt to metamorphose into sky”; even at its foothills, the world’s tallest mountain range feels otherworldly and awe-inspiring, befitting a place that has long been the backdrop for mythical tales of spirituality and wonder.
Peel away the Orientalist mysticism, however, and a much more grounded — yet no less sublime — picture of the region emerges.

The Himalayas span five countries: Nepal, India, China, Bhutan, and Pakistan. In India alone, the range covers 13 states and union territories, from the disputed region of Kashmir to Himachal Pradesh, home to Shimla, the summer capital of the British Raj.
In the latter state, agriculture and, increasingly, hydropower anchor the economy, with tourism a significant contributor.
And as of 2023, Himachal Pradesh is also home to India’s most ambitious restaurant: NAAR.
Perched at the edge of a cliff above the pine forest, NAAR is part of Amaya, a 25-acre boutique hotel near the remote village of Darwa in the Solan district of Himachal Pradesh.
Few would dispute the description: Kasauli, the nearest town, is 45 minutes away, while the closest airport, in Chandigarh, is a two-and-a-half-hour drive down hairpin bends on steep dirt roads.
NAAR, the Kashmiri word for fire, is Chef Prateek Sadhu’s ode to Himalayan produce and cooking.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

After working at some of the most illustrious restaurants around the world and opening one of the best restaurants in India, Chef Prateek Sadhu decided to head up into the Himalayas, which inspired him to open NAAR. — Picture by Pankaj Anand, courtesy of NAAR
A native of Kashmir, Sadhu trained at the Culinary Institute of America before working in the kitchens of Alinea, The French Laundry, Le Bernardin and Noma.
In 2016, he returned to India to open Masque in Mumbai, where he introduced diners to deeply regional cooking rooted in the produce and traditions of Kashmir.
Under him, the restaurant ranked No. 21 on Asia’s 50 Best Restaurants list in 2022 and was named the best restaurant in India that year.
That year, at the height of Masque’s acclaim, Sadhu quit and headed for the Himalayas in search of inspiration.
A year later, NAAR opened. “It was a gamble,” Aashina Kaul, Sadhu’s wife, who runs the restaurant’s operations, told me.
“We were afraid that nobody would be crazy enough to come all the way out here for a meal.”
During my visit on a Tuesday afternoon, the 16-seater restaurant was full, and the busy season hadn’t started yet.

Sadhu told me October typically marks the beginning of it, when affluent Indians travel from across the country to the luxury developments around the region — Shimla is particularly popular — for a winter getaway.

Recognition is arriving alongside the crowds: earlier this year, NAAR ranked No. 30 on Asia’s 50 Best Restaurants list, and this week, Condé Nast Traveller India named it the number one restaurant in India.
The 14-course meal (6,800 INR, RM287) begins with cocktails and snacks at the salon, a small building separate from the main restaurant.
Berries, mushrooms and, unsurprisingly, pines make up the base of many tinctures and liquors, but so does trout.
Though the fish isn’t native to India, it has thrived in Kashmir’s glacial streams since the British introduced it in 1900.

It appears in five courses across the menu, but my first taste of it came in a cocktail: charcoal-filtered tequila infused with smoked trout bone, a pickle of stone fruit, garlic and mustard seed, and trout bone bitters.
It went down like a guilty pleasure cigarette and a filthy martini at the same time, which is to say, wonderfully.
The first snack, a bhangjeera leaf fritter with tomato jhol (a thin gravy) and tomato seed chutney, sets the distinct anise flavour of a perilla leaf against the tang of tomatoes.
Trout reappeared in the second, which Sadhu described as a “trout belly sandwich”. Cubes of trout dressed in a chutney of sorrel and fresh chilli are tucked into a thin, crisp buckwheat flatbread.
A significant crop across the Indian subcontinent, buckwheat is particularly associated with festivals like Shivratri and Janmashtami, when fasting Hindus eat only food made from its flour.
A Kashmiri tujj followed. Typically a skewer of grilled mutton, NAAR’s version uses lamb rump, brined overnight, then grilled with a mustard and chilli glaze.
The onion emulsion served alongside cushions the char and heat of the meat like an allium pillow.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

A cocktail made from trout bones (left). ‘Tujj’ is a popular Kashmiri grilled skewer. At NAAR, lamb rump is brined, then glazed and grilled and served with an onion emulsion (right). — Photos by Ethan Lau
Next came askalu, a Himachali snack that resembles a mini deep-fried doughnut.
Traditionally made with rice flour, NAAR’s uses tapioca instead, and is stuffed with duck and topped with a golden raspberry and mountain pepper masala.
The berry, which came into season that week, is much sweeter than its red counterpart.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Golden raspberries, which come into season in September (left). Inside the restaurant at sunset (right). — Picture courtesy of NAAR
We were moved into the main restaurant for the rest of the meal, where the dark synths of Depeche Mode replaced the funky screeching of James Brown at the salon.

Though the restaurant’s reverence for foraging and hyper-seasonal produce could easily come across as lofty and high-minded, there was a playfulness to the way the team moved and interacted with guests.
Less like self-serious acolytes of a new-age cult, more like curious, earnest children at the best summer camp in the world, if those children were skilled cooks and servers.
A quartet of trout courses followed a bowl of corn custard paired with a chewy sabudana bread, or, as we know it better in Malaysia, sago.

The course that left the most lasting impression was the one where I could recognise every component: a layer of smoked trout roe, glistening under the sun, on an unlikely bed of salted banana custard and banana honey.
The banana’s sweetness stayed on my tongue between bursts of salty roe, opening my mind to an entirely new way of experiencing sweet and salty.

Next came trout trimmings in a crisp, refreshing broth of raw mango and green apple, topped with a dill foam, and then “Dirty Toast”, on the menu since NAAR opened and named for the mess it leaves behind.
A wedge of sourdough inspired by Ladakhi khambir is laden with apple and chilli chutney, onion jus and a Himalayan mustard sauce, and crowned with a thick hunk of lightly charred trout.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->

‘Dirty Toast’ has been on the menu since NAAR opened (left). — Picture courtesy of NAAR. ‘Sundarkala’ is a type of hand-rolled noodle from Uttarakhand, a state that borders Tibet (right). — Picture by Pankaj Anand, courtesy of NAAR
No shade to the lox and bagels and tuna melts of the world, but I doubt I’m topping this anytime soon.
The quartet closed with a portion of trout belly in a curry of trout bones and pickled chillies, to be lapped up with tilvor.
Known as “the Kashmiri bagel” for its shape, tilvor has sesame and poppy seeds sprinkled over a crusty exterior that gives way, when torn, to a soft interior.
And then there was a bowl of noodles. Sundarkala are a type of hand-rolled noodle from Uttarakhand, a state to the east of Himachal Pradesh that borders Tibet.
Traditionally made with finger millet and wheat, NAAR’s uses buckwheat instead. Thin and flat like cu mian (thick wheat noodles) but without the alkaline spring, they had a tender bite.
They sat in a broth made with timur, a brighter, more citrusy cousin to the Sichuan peppercorn, alongside lamb gyurma, a Tibetan blood sausage.
Meaty depth meets a citrusy, numbing tingle, with buckwheat noodles playing matchmaker.
By the time the penultimate course rolled around family-style, almost three hours had passed and I hadn’t felt a second of it.
Two dishes flanked a large pot of rice infused with tomato chutney: a mild, cream-coloured yoghurt curry with foraged morels, and barbecued pork with a pumpkin seed sauce.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
The view from the restaurant. — Picture courtesy of NAAR
Sadhu made a point of telling us he wouldn’t tell us how to eat it, though he hadn’t for any of the earlier courses either.

This one needed telling least of all. I spooned hunks of tender pork and meaty morels onto my rice, the spongy caps releasing the rich yoghurt curry all over my plate, then zhuzhed it all up with a few teaspoons of NAAR’s house hot sauce.
A sorbet of sea buckthorn, a very, very sour berry, with timur custard, orange oil and honeycomb cleared the way for a finale of pickled peach with almond cream.
Both were sharp and satisfying, though by then the meal had begun to blur.
NAAR had taken my taste buds on a whirlwind through a famously mythicised region, one specific ingredient and tradition at a time.

I had touched the berries, smelled the shrubs and eaten the leaves, all tangible, and yet, without much context for the centuries of history and millions of people behind them, I felt myself sink into awe.
Afterwards, outside, all I could do was look up at the sky, which felt only slightly out of reach, and my mind began to wander — and wonder.
NAAR
VPO Darwa, Sub Tehsil-Kishangarh,
Kasauli, District Solan,
Himachal Pradesh, India
Open Tuesday to Sunday, 12.30pm—3pm, 6.30pm—11pm
https://restaurantnaar.com

f24dbaa7fcecb135: PETALING JAYA: PAS should allocate one-third of the seats in the four states it governs to Umno if the two parties want to continue working together in future elections, says Umno Supreme Council member Nur Jazlan Mohamed.

Nur Jazlan said PAS did not need to contest every seat in Terengganu, Kelantan, Kedah and Perlis, arguing that a two-thirds share would be enough, pointing out that BN’s two-thirds majority in Johor in 2022 had boosted investor confidence.
Nur Jazlan, who is also Pulai Umno chief, contrasted this with Terengganu, which he described as rich in oil, but "nobody says foreign investors are flocking there".

“So PAS needs to consider this. It does not need to contest 100% of the seats, only two-thirds. If it wants to strengthen its position, what is wrong with allocating one-third of the seats in those states to its Umno partners?
"That would demonstrate that PAS has confidence in Malay unity and is sincere in pursuing it," Utusan Malaysia quoted him as saying.
PAS won all 27 seats it contested in Terengganu, 37 of the 45 seats in Kelantan, 21 of 36 seats in Kedah and nine seats in Perlis.
Umno and PAS have gradually renewed their political cooperation, beginning with an indirect understanding to avoid clashes in Johor before evolving into an informal electoral pact in Negeri Sembilan.
The two parties are now discussing possible electoral cooperation in the upcoming Melaka state election. Leaders from both parties have also attended each other’s general assemblies.
On concerns that cooperation with PAS could alienate Chinese voters, Nur Jazlan said Umno could play a key role in improving PAS’s image among non-Malays.
“The main problem non-Malay voters have with PAS is that they are not confident they will be given the freedom to live their lives.
“I think PAS can be flexible, too. But its flexibility will be influenced by its cooperation with Umno. So Umno plays a big role in softening PAS’s image in the future."
Nur Jazlan said his own research showed Chinese support for Umno in Johor had returned to about 20%, which he attributed to confidence in the state leadership’s handling of the economy and jobs.

"They look at whether a political party can provide them with a better life and greater well-being, and will vote for it if it can. This is despite the many prejudices associated with parties such as Umno and PAS," he added.
079e082487a0dd9f: NEW YORK: New York's subway is known for being dirty, noisy and sometimes flooded, but that doesn't stop people from flocking to grab a seat, sign or other memorabilia at a unique annual auction.
In south Brooklyn, shoppers hoping to get a slice of the city's transit service waited for hours to trawl through an open-air market organised by city authorities.
Each person gets a maximum of 45 minutes to search, allowing others to come in after them.
Nori Juba, 61, found what he was looking for: a large sign bearing the name of Grand Central station, along with the numbers of the subway lines he takes every day.
The train system is "old and creaky and it's outdated," he admitted.

"But I think that's what makes it interesting. And this piece of metal is dirty. It smells like a subway station, but there's something about it that makes it real New York, one of a kind in the world."
The prices aren't cheap: a medium-sized sign cost around US$500, while larger ones can run past US$1,000.
The iconic orange plastic seats from the New York subway go for around US$900 each.
Celebrities are sometimes spotted at the market, and this month New York resident and filmmaker Spike Lee was stopping for pictures with fellow shoppers.
He proudly showed off the metal sign he just bought, marked "Penn Station," the subway stop for Madison Square Garden – the arena where his beloved Knicks basketball team plays.
"I don't take the subway anymore to the big games," he confessed to reporters, but recalled riding the train regularly while growing up – noting he always paid his fare.
"I never jumped the turnstile either. Let the record state!" he joked.
New York's Metropolitan Transportation Authority has always resold its signs to collectors but more recently opened up sales to the public, said Paul Dvoskin, the director in charge of the programme.
"Five years ago, an idea was born to hold a garage sale of sorts, and to let people just come in and purchase these items" in person, he said.
"We called it a grab-and-go back then, and it just ended up being significantly more popular than we ever thought it would be."
Officials do not disclose how much the two-day sale brings in, but it draws around 4,000 people each year.
The plastic seats, sold only since last year, are the most popular items.
So are the MetroCards, the small yellow magnetic cards emblematic of the city, which have recently been retired from use – they sell for US$6.
With a budget of US$70, Trinyce and Ijeoma, two women in their 20s, said they were trying to find something to decorate their apartment.
"I'd like a piece of New York to represent my living space, like as a representation of me," Ijeoma said.

eb72bc97ec45f159: KUALA LUMPUR: The 2027 Budget's extension of the income tax exemption and fixed stamp duty rates on ship financing is expected to ease financing constraints for Malaysian shipowners facing stringent collateral requirements and mismatches between loan tenures and ships' useful lives.

Maritime analyst Nazery Khalid said the two incentives announced under 2027 Budget could lower ship financing costs, particularly for vessels built locally, while creating more favourable conditions for the development of domestic shipping capacity.

Prime Minister and Finance Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced the extension of the full income tax exemption for Malaysian shipping companies until the year of assessment 2036 when tabling 2027 Budget, themed "Reaching for the Skies, While Anchored On Our Values", in the Dewan Rakyat on Friday.

The government also introduced fixed stamp duty rates on loans for the purchase or construction of Malaysian vessels, at RM2,000 for loans of up to RM100 million and RM5,000 for loans exceeding RM100 million.

"These measures could support the development of local shipping capacity in key sectors such as energy, bulk commodities and container shipping, helping to cater to Malaysia's growing trade volumes and economic growth," Nazery told Bernama when met after a panel discussion titled "Strengthening Malaysia's Downstream Petroleum Value Chain and Identifying Gaps and Enabling Factors", organised by Maritime Network Sdn Bhd and Universiti Malaysia Terengganu (UMT) here today.

He also said the incentives could also reduce Malaysia's reliance on foreign vessels and limit foreign exchange outflows, while addressing longstanding requests by local shipowners for more supportive financing conditions.

The incentives could also help shipping companies, particularly smaller operators, accelerate digitalisation to remain competitive amid geopolitical uncertainty, major shifts in global supply chains and rising energy costs.

Nazery said shipping companies also needed to invest in modern vessels with environmentally friendly features to meet the International Maritime Organisation's (IMO) requirements to reduce greenhouse gas emissions, in line with the country's net-zero ambitions.

He said this when met after a panel discussion titled "Strengthening Malaysia's Downstream Petroleum Value Chain and Identifying Gaps and Enabling Factors", organised by Maritime Network Sdn Bhd and Universiti Malaysia Terengganu (UMT) here today.
INCREASE IN TRAINING BERTHS FOR MARITIME CADETS

Nazery pointed out that cadets from Malaysian maritime academies, including the Malaysian Maritime Academy, faced difficulties securing berths on commercial vessels to obtain the practical seagoing experience required to qualify as professional seafarers.

He proposed that the government consider linking access to financing from government-owned financial institutions, such as Bank Pembangunan Malaysia Bhd and Export-Import Bank of Malaysia Bhd (EXIM Bank), or special maritime funds allocated under the national budget, to the provision of training berths for cadets.

"If the government could gazette a requirement for shipping companies in Malaysia to provide training berths for cadets, it would address a long-standing need and be greatly appreciated, not only by maritime academies in Malaysia but also by the cadets themselves.
"However, this is clearly a commercial decision that the government may not be able to impose on them," said Nazery.

He said that this measure could help alleviate the shortage of training berths while encouraging more young Malaysians to pursue careers at sea, knowing that opportunities for obtaining the necessary onboard training would be available.
94c3fbcc286850d6: KUALA LUMPUR: There are no reports of Malaysian casualties following the latest attack on Saudi Arabia’s King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and a projectile falling in the vicinity of King Fahd International Airport in Dammam on Saturday, the foreign ministry said.

In a statement, the ministry also known as Wisma Putra, said the Malaysian embassy in Riyadh was in contact with several Malaysians stranded by the travel disruptions and was providing the necessary consular assistance.
“Malaysians residing in, travelling through, or planning to travel to Saudi Arabia are strongly urged to remain vigilant.

“In view of the ongoing flight disruptions, those with upcoming travel plans are advised to verify their flight status directly with their respective airlines before proceeding to the airports,” it said in a statement today.

The ministry also advised Malaysians to anticipate possible delays or cancellations, and to stay informed through official channels and strictly adhere to safety instructions issued by local authorities.
Following the incident, Saudi Arabia's civil aviation authority announced the temporary suspension of operations at King Khalid International Airport.

To ensure timely communication and access to consular support, Wisma Putra urged Malaysians to register and regularly update their contact details via the e-Konsular portal at https://ekonsular.kln.gov.my.

For immediate consular assistance or emergencies, Malaysians may contact the Malaysian embassy in Riyadh at 00 966 11 488 7098 / 00 966 11 488 7100 for general enquiries, or the emergency helpline at 00 966 56 300 6319 after office hours, or via email mwriyadh@kln.gov.my.
Wisma Putra said it will continue to monitor the developments closely and provide further updates as necessary.
It was previously reported that 12 people were killed and more than 300 injured in Saturday’s attack on the King Khalid International Airport.
Four Saudi citizens, two Bangladeshi nationals, and one each from the US, Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Palestine, and Sudan were killed in the attack.
24746b2eb3c3348e: PETALING JAYA: Wisma Putra mengesahkan tiada rakyat Malaysia terkorban atau cedera dalam serangan di Lapangan Terbang Antarabangsa Raja Khalid di Riyadh, Arab Saudi, semalam.

Wisma Putra berkata, Kedutaan Besar Malaysia di Riyadh sedang berhubung dengan beberapa rakyat Malaysia yang dalam perjalanan dan terkandas bagi memberikan bantuan konsular susulan penggantungan sementara operasi di lapangan terbang berkenaan.

"Kementerian Luar sedang memantau rapat situasi susulan serangan terbaharu itu serta laporan sebuah projektil jatuh berhampiran Lapangan Terbang Antarabangsa Raja Fadh di Dammam," katanya dalam kenyataan.
Pada masa sama, Wisma Putra menggesa rakyat Malaysia yang menetap, dalam perjalanan transit atau merancang ke Arab Saudi supaya sentiasa berwaspada.

"Memandangkan gangguan penerbangan masih berterusan, mereka yang mempunyai rancangan perjalanan dalam masa terdekat dinasihat mengesahkan status penerbangan secara langsung dengan syarikat penerbangan sebelum ke lapangan terbang.

"Rakyat Malaysia turut dinasihatkan bersedia menghadapi kemungkinan kelewatan atau pembatalan penerbangan, sentiasa mengikuti perkembangan melalui saluran rasmi serta mematuhi sepenuhnya arahan keselamatan pihak berkuasa tempatan."

Bagi memastikan komunikasi dapat dilaksanakan dengan segera serta memudahkan penyaluran bantuan konsular, Wisma Putra menggesa rakyat Malaysia mendaftar dan sentiasa mengemas kini maklumat melalui https://ekonsular.kln.gov.my.

Bagi mendapatkan bantuan konsular segera atau dalam situasi kecemasan, rakyat Malaysia boleh menghubungi Kedutaan Besar Malaysia di Riyadh melalui 00 966 11 488 7098 / 00 966 11 488 7100 atau talian kecemasan 00 966 56 300 6319 (selepas waktu pejabat) atau e-mel mwriyadh@kln.gov.my.
98f485f50ccd2f35: VISAKHAPATNAM: Handcuffs encircle Google's logo on one campaign poster, while another warns that people "cannot drink data", as opposition mounts to the tech giant's planned AI mega-facility in India.
Excavators have swung into action, clearing forest and farmland on the southeast coast for the US$15 billion construction of Google's largest data centre outside the US.
The project at Visakhapatnam in Andhra Pradesh state, a port often called Vizag, is championed by India as a cornerstone of its technological ambitions.
But many residents fear the data centre -- one of several huge new tech sites in Vizag -- will strain water and power resources, damage the environment and bring too few jobs in return.
Farmer Chandala Sadamma told AFP that when she sees the red-earth scars where her plot of mango and cashew trees once stood, "I feel like crying".
She was paid more than US$82,000 for the two-acre (0.8-hectare) stretch of land, but the transaction left a bitter taste.
"Some company came and, without showing any respect, they took the land and we accepted it," the 50-year-old said.
Vizag is a landing point for submarine internet cables linking the country to Singapore, so for India, the location of the 600-acre site -- more than 340 football pitches -- is ideal.
The "AI Hub investment is a multi-decade commitment" carrying "an obligation to be a good neighbour", said Alexander Smith, Google's head of infrastructure and energy for Asia-Pacific.
"The watershed, the grid and the communities around our facilities must be better off for our being here."
The Andhra Pradesh government told AFP that in addition to financial compensation, new housing is being built and handed over to people who had lived on the site.
'Why here?'
Governments and tech firms worldwide are spending trillions of dollars on data centres -- boxy buildings stuffed with racks of computer servers that power apps and AI tools.
But the developments have sparked backlash in many countries, with a Finnish authority recently ordering work to halt on two Google data centre sites pending mandatory environmental assessments.
Activists in Andhra Pradesh are also demanding a moratorium on new data centres across the state until independent environmental and social impact evaluations are published.
"The United States has a huge coast... They can simply set it up there," Gutta Rohith of the local campaign group Human Rights Forum told AFP at a meeting of around 150 people.
"Why are they coming here?"
Opposition to data centres, including in the United States, often takes aim at the use of local water resources to cool hot servers down.
Google said it will use "advanced" air cooling technology instead at the India hub, while the state plans six 1.2-gigawatt nuclear power plants as energy demand soars.
Still, water use worries residents, especially given plans for Vizag to become a tech megahub.
"They are saying that Google is being established for the education and employment opportunities of our children," said shopkeeper Gubbala Ramanamma.
But "we are already struggling with water scarcity", the 57-year-old said, standing beside a dry well.
Land prices

Google said its data centre will generate US$688 million in local economic activity each year and support about 4,200 jobs during construction, with hundreds of specialist jobs once operational in 2028.
Andhra Pradesh's government also said it expects "188,000 direct and indirect jobs to be generated".
But Rohith said the economic benefits would not necessarily trickle down from the warehouse-like facilities.
"We need mass employment and labour-intensive industries, not high-capital industries."
Google is not alone -- a joint venture between Reliance Industries, Brookfield and Digital Realty is investing US$11 billion in another AI data centre in Vizag.

Land prices have risen by an average of "more than 45 percent" since the city unveiled its development plans, said E. Ashok Kumar, Visakhapatnam head of the Confederation of Real Estate Developers' Associations of India.
Meanwhile, as AI use accelerates, the world's most populous nation has rolled out incentives to attract big tech companies, including tax cuts.
Despite its widespread internet and app use generating nearly a fifth of the world's digital data, India has only about three percent of global data-centre capacity, government figures show.

Andhra Pradesh Technology Minister Nara Lokesh, in an interview with AFP in February, spoke of investment agreements worth US$175 billion involving 760 projects -- and vowed to "execute these projects at a pace that the country has never seen".
Lokesh has also insisted that "residential requirements will always be prioritised over data centres", according to a statement.
"The water needs of our people will always come first."
Visakhapatnam environmental campaigner E.A.S. Sarma, a former senior government official who worked in the power and finance ministries, has called for a water audit by an independent agency.
"Civilisations have vanished because of water shortages," he warned.
f6bfdaa84dba48ce: SINGAPORE, Oct 11 — A Chinese tourist received a rude welcome to Singapore when his Louis Vuitton bag got stolen at Gardens by the Bay during his first visit to the country.
He managed to track the alleged thief and retrieve it within 20 minutes, but several of the items inside were gone.
User Lao Hei Livefree posted on Xiaohongshu: “It was truly an extraordinary trip. My first time abroad, even my first time leaving the country, my first time in Singapore, and I got robbed!”
Photos accompanying the post show him walking around Gardens by the Bay with a police officer, and at least three officers at the scene talking to him and handling his luxury handbag.
He also received a card from the police stating they would investigate it further.
Found the alleged thief by chance
Over several posts, Lao Hei Livefree explained that the alleged theft happened at around 9pm on Oct 5 after he saw a light show at the Supertree grove with his friends.
He had left his bag behind him and leaned forward to discuss the itinerary with them, but heard “a burst of rapid footsteps”.
Turning around, he discovered his bag was gone.
The tourist then tried to track it down using his wireless earphones to no avail. But figuring “the thief couldn’t have gone far”, he started walking towards an exit to block his path.
“Just then, I bumped into someone and waved my hand to ask for directions, but he took off running,” he added.
Suspicious, he gave chase and snatched a paper bag back from that man, only to find his luxury handbag inside.
The tourist discovered that some of its contents including his passport, pocket camera and livestreaming equipment were gone.
Even a sock he had left inside was missing, but an eyewitness told him that he had seen someone with his pocket camera and the rest of his belongings stuffed into the sock.
Lao Hei Livefree claimed that the alleged thief, who was dressed suspiciously in a black headscarf, managed to get away, disappearing into some bushes.
While he did not seem particularly bothered about the money lost, the tourist said he was concerned about getting his passport back.
Coordinated theft?
Lao Hei Livefree said that he believes that the thief wasn’t acting alone, and part of a “gang”.
He also believes the man he caught may not have been the person who stole his bag either, but just there to collect the stolen items.
Claiming to have reviewed CCTV footage from Gardens by the Bay, the tourist said that the man had avoided cameras while in the park.
He had also allegedly parked at an area designated for buses, and entered through an exit and exited through an entrance.
“In this way, the surveillance cameras couldn’t capture his license plate,” the Xiaohongshu user explained.
He added that the CCTV footage allegedly showed the man park, open his car boot and leave.
When he returned, he appeared to toss something into the boot, close it and leave Gardens by the Bay, which makes him believe he was only there to pick up the stolen items.
The tourist added that he hoped other vehicles on the road have dashcam footage showing the getaway car’s license plate number to help with the police investigation.
However, as of posting his video on October 8, he had not received further updates from the police.
In response to AsiaOne’s queries, the Singapore Police Force confirmed that a report was lodged and investigations are ongoing. — AsiaOne

5909ec5dd41dd59a: UNITED NATIONS: UN secretary-general Antonio Guterres late Saturday strongly condemned a Houthi attack targeting the main airport in the Saudi capital Riyadh, which claimed at least 12 lives and injured hundreds of civilians, Anadolu Ajansi reported.

83dd41286bec4587: SINGAPORE, Oct 11 — An American man living in Singapore refused to pay rent for a semi-detached property he rented in Kembangan, yet sued its elderly owners when they attempted to re-enter the house.

According to a judgement from Oct 5, the applications made by Anthony Thomas Price were dismissed by District Judge Chiah Kok Khun who said he had “devised a deliberate scheme” to rent the home without intending to pay rent.
The tenancy agreement was made by Price using a Singapore-incorporated private company with paid-up capital of only S$200 (RM638), with himself and his family as directors.
The company was also the applicant of the claim.

Chiah argued that Price had a pattern of “using shell companies to rent landed properties in Singapore for his family to stay and not paying rent” and embroiling defendants in litigation “in a bid to extend his period of unlawful occupation” of the homes he rented.
“In my view, the claimant’s applications are filed in plain abuse of process of the court,” he added.
The counterclaim the elderly homeowners in their 80s made against Price was also allowed.
‘Plain breach’ of tenancy agreement
According to the judgement, a tenancy agreement was signed in April for two years, from May 1, 2026 to April 30, 2028, with rent of S$7,500 to be paid on the first day of each month.
If rent remained unpaid for seven days, an interest rate of 10 per cent per annum applied, calculated from the due date to the date of actual payment.
Price had only paid rent for the first month.
Thus, the district judge concluded that Price was in “clear breach of the tenancy agreement … in refusing to pay rent”.
This also gave the defendants, the elderly homeowners, the “rights of re-entry” to take back their property.
On top of this, Price breached further tenancy agreements when he paid only half the security deposit of S$15,000 when he moved in and refused to pay the remainder due on June 1.

Price and his family also refused to set up an account and pay for utilities, which they were obliged to in their tenancy agreement, and installed CCTV cameras without obtaining the landlords’ written consent, going against the tenancy agreement.
Price had attempted to justify his refusal to pay rent based on alleged defects to the property, involving “approximately 35 repair, rectification or practical occupation issues”.

He claimed that it was “not a straightforward rent-only matter” and disputed the homeowners’ entitlement to “rely on [claimant’s failure to pay rent and other sums] to take possession by self-help, particularly in the context of the unresolved repair, safety, tenantability and quiet enjoyment issues”.
But Chiah dismissed these, calling them “worthless words and a roundabout way” to say Price refused to pay rent.
“If the claimant is serious about its assertions regarding the condition of the premises, it is for the claimant to pursue its assertions separately against the defendants,” he added.
“It cannot use these assertions as an excuse not to pay rent.”
Defendants ‘fully entitled to their counterclaim’
The homeowners made an attempt “at peaceful re-entry” into the Kembangan home on June 29, but were resisted by Price and his family.
However, Chiah concluded that, in view of the claimant’s refusal to pay rent, the tenancy agreements give the homeowners “a contractual right to re-enter the premises and terminate the lease”.

He also allowed their counterclaim on basis of arrears of rent — S$22,500 between June and August and an interest of S$269.17— and the remaining S$7,500 of the security deposit, as well as $813.74 for utilities.

In addition, Chiah said: “The claimant is to reimburse the defendants in respect of any unexpired part of the tenancy, a proportionate part of the commission of S$8,175 that was paid by the defendants to the estate agent.”
He also allowed the defendants to claim double rent, calculated from Aug 15 until Price and his family hands over the vacant home.
Chiah ordered a fixed cost of S$15,000 plus disbursements of S$2,031.98 to be paid by the claimant to the defendants as well.
Not the only time
Price had used shell companies twice before to attempt to live in landed properties without paying rent.
In 2019, he had used the same shell company that signed the tenancy agreement for the Kembangan property, to rent a landed property at Jalan Selamat.
He also used a wholly-owned subsidiary of his shell company to enter a one-year tenancy agreement with the owner of a landed property at Burnfoot Terrace in 2024.
In both cases, he only paid part of the security deposit and stopped paying rent after a few months, and the owners of both properties had taken him to court over it.
Price and his family had lived in the Jalan Selamat property for at least five months, and at the Burnfoot Terrace home for nearly a year.
While the case regarding the Jalan Selamat home was eventually settled, the proceedings for the Burnfoot Terrace property are still ongoing. — AsiaOne
baa73ea6ce685f78: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 11 — The government’s payment of Special Financial Assistance (BKK) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) Madani next year, in conjunction with the 70th anniversary of the country’s independence, is an appreciation for the people’s role in Malaysia’s development since independence.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the tujuh dasawarsa (seven decades) of independence is significant because independence itself represented a gift to the people.
“The tujuh dasarwasa of independence represents a gift to the people,” he told Bernama when asked about its significance, which was mentioned in his Budget 2027 speech on Friday.
Under Budget 2027, the government has agreed to provide RM1,500 in BKK to 1.3 million civil servants in Grade Utama B and below, including contract staff.
More than one million government pensioners, including veterans with and without pensions, will also receive RM750 in assistance.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said the BKK payments will be made in two instalments, before Aidilfitri and ahead of the 70th anniversary of independence.
Malaysians aged 18 and above who do not receive the Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) will also receive RM100 per payment under Sara Madani, disbursed twice.

The assistance is intended to ensure that the benefits of national development reach the public and to acknowledge the contributions of civil servants, pensioners and the wider community since Malaysia gained independence.
Malaysia will celebrate 70 years of independence in 2027, marking seven decades of progress and efforts to improve the wellbeing of its people.

Budget 2027, themed “Reaching for the Sky, Rooted in the Ground”, was tabled with a government allocation of RM459.8 billion, supplemented by RM25 billion in investments from government-linked investment companies, RM11 billion in public-private investments, and RM14.2 billion from federal statutory bodies and Minister of Finance Incorporated (MOF Inc) companies.
This brings the total size of Budget 2027, which continues an expansionary fiscal policy, to RM510 billion.

The fifth Madani Budget seeks to ensure that resilient economic growth delivers tangible benefits to the people, including better wages, more effective targeted support, stronger fiscal discipline and a faster transition to higher-value industries. — Bernama
b9ccc69255a21123: NORTH JACKSON (United States), Oct 11 — For Doug Rende, who runs an aluminium product manufacturer in the US state of Ohio, President Donald Trump’s tariffs have meant millions of dollars more in annual costs — and recently, the Iran war has made shipments even more expensive.
Rende is chief executive at Shapes Unlimited, one of many American producers smarting from Trump’s economic policies as midterm elections approach.
“Frustrating would be one word,” Rende told AFP.
“And I think that we’re sensing a lack of trust in not only the administration but the governmental process, the role of Congress to rein in executive power,” he added.
Since returning to the presidency in January 2025, Trump has wielded executive authority to slap tariffs on various products and countries.
Besides aluminum, the duties hit steel and autos too, while US trading partners face additional tariffs that vary by country.
Even as some American manufacturers have benefited as their foreign competitors encounter higher barriers, others struggle with ballooning costs and persistent uncertainty.
Trump’s spiraling trade fight with Canada and war with Iran have only deepened worries.
Grievances over Trump’s trade policies are among fault lines that Democrats hope will work in their favor as they push to flip control of the Senate and House of Representatives in November’s vote.
Tough to cope
Rende’s company in North Jackson, Ohio, makes and distributes aluminum building products used in fixtures like fences.
Trump’s tariffs on aluminium have steadily climbed, from 10 per cent during his first presidency to 25 per cent and then 50 per cent last year, and Rende has felt the impact.
“This year alone, it’s upwards of US$4.5 million (RM18.4 million) to US$5 million in additional costs,” Rende said.
“There’s only so much that the end consumer is willing to eat,” he added. “So, we absorb a healthy portion.”
These added costs include steeper transportation fees, as fuel prices surged with the US-Israel war on Iran. Surcharges are “upwards of US$6,500 per container” of goods from suppliers, Rende said.
As a result, he has paused recruitment for new jobs while investing in more robotic assembly.

Sam Miller, another Ohio manufacturer who makes kitchen and bathroom products, has been hit on both fronts in Trump’s trade wars, paying tariffs on imported materials from Asia while finding it harder to expand into Canada because of trade tensions.

“It’s been difficult for businesses to manage,” Miller told AFP from his factory floor in Warren as a machine hummed nearby, cutting countertop material. “I do think that there will be a shift away from Republican views.”
Although Miller received refunds after the Supreme Court struck down many of Trump’s duties, the US leader has since reinstated many of them.
‘Straining’
Deteriorating US-Canada ties add to his challenges, with Washington and Ottawa slapping tariffs on each other’s products after trade negotiations collapsed in August.
“We’re selling into Canada and it is particularly straining on both us and our customers,” Miller said.
He originally planned on opening a distribution facility in Canada this year, but progress has slowed.
Guy Coviello, president of the Youngstown Warren Regional Chamber, told AFP he is monitoring tariffs, the Iran war and immigration very closely.
These are a “mixed bag” for firms but negative overall, said Coviello, whose business group has some 3,000 members.
Some firms have lost customers or had to downsize, he said.
Canada is also Ohio’s biggest export market, with a third of Ohio’s exports going to the country.
“Where it gets even more complicated is that there are some goods that go back and forth across the border multiple times,” he said.
The Iran war adds to stresses, raising freight costs and hitting aluminum supplies due to drone attacks in the Middle East.
With a lack of new US aluminum smelters, Coviello said: “We are all for tariffs for critical items such as defense and medical industry.”
But he added: “We have to be careful when you’re talking about products that are not crucial and are not available in the US.” — AFP
a1604e5270e24c1f: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — King Abdullah II of Jordan will undertake a two-day state visit to Malaysia from Sunday at the invitation of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia.
In a statement, the Foreign Ministry also known as Wisma Putra, said this will be King Abdullah II’s second state visit to Malaysia since May 2008.
“The state visit comes as Malaysia and Jordan commemorate over six decades of diplomatic relations, established in 1965,” the statement read.

The Jordanian king will be accompanied by Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs and Expatriates Ayman Safadi, as well as senior officials from the Royal Hashemite Court and the government.
During the visit, King Abdullah II will be accorded a state welcoming ceremony at Istana Negara, followed by an audience with Sultan Ibrahim.
King Abdullah II will also attend a state banquet and is scheduled to have an audience with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim
Malaysia and Jordan share close and longstanding ties, particularly in the field of education.

According to Wisma Putra, as of 2026, there are 1,636 Malaysian students studying at higher education institutions in Jordan and over 1,490 Jordanian students studying at Malaysian higher education institutions.

“Both countries continue to promote educational exchanges, academic collaboration and the sharing of expertise, while strengthening cooperation in higher education and scientific research,” the statement said.

Wisma Putra noted that, beyond these longstanding people-to-people ties, the two countries share a common commitment to advancing peace, justice, and lasting stability in the West Asia region, especially in support of the legitimate rights of the Palestinian people.

Bilateral trade between Malaysia and Jordan reached RM993.4 million in 2025, an increase of 15.2 per cent from 2024, and grew by a further 8.0 per cent to RM740.7 million from January to August 2026, compared with the corresponding period in 2025, it added. — Bernama
8595c9db9b41283e: TEHRAN: At a Tehran bazaar where fragrant herbs and spices whet the appetite, shopkeeper Nasir says locals once bought his nuts by the kilo but soaring prices caused by the US-Iran war have eaten into sales, leaving businesses fighting for survival.

The marketplace in the Iranian capital's north would usually be abuzz with customers, but shops now sit mostly empty with only small numbers of people walking its old narrow paths, a jarring shift for the sellers shouting to promote their goods.
"There used to be customers who bought two to five kilograms. Now, they're down to buying one kilogram or half a kilogram," said the 61-year-old.
"Prices are truly high. We all know it, and it would be a lie to say otherwise."
Nasir called on authorities to stabilise the currency so businesses could plan ahead.
"We're left in limbo, everyone is," said the fruit and nut seller.
"They need to stabilise the dollar exchange rate."

Iran's economy has been battered by years of sanctions, but the conflict that began in February with US-Israeli attacks and an American blockade of the country's ports has put extra strain on daily life.

Rising inflation, nearly 90% year-on-year in September according to official figures, and erratic currency exchange fluctuations have driven up the cost of everyday items. Food prices have more than doubled since last year.

At the bazaar, a historic covered market in Tehran's Tajrish square, locals surrounded by Iranian flags and Persian signage try to escape the economic gloom, scanning sweets, jewellery, traditional garments and cuts of meat before their weekend begins.
In an alley, a street artist plays a guitar while another drums his hands on a box to draw tips from passersby.
'Just need stability'
But across the commercial district, many struggle to see a future for their businesses.

"It is a desperate, last-ditch struggle. Manufacturers are going bankrupt, laying off staff and closing shops, and the impact inevitably reaches us," said Ali Nowruzi, 36, who runs a sportswear shop in the bazaar.
The businessman now orders only a few items for display on his shop's shelves to stop them from looking bare like his warehouse, which he says lies empty due to lack of demand.
"We have absolutely no plan for the future. When people don't come to buy... it effectively spells bankruptcy for the business," he said, citing rising rent and utility bills.
"We just need some stability."
Many shoppers, whose purchasing power has weakened since the outbreak of war, are seen leaving the bazaar without buying anything.
Azadeh, a 45-year-old woman currently out of work, says she just goes there to "watch the shops".
Mounting pressure over the war saw Iran's GDP contract 10.1% year-on-year between late March and late June, according to official figures.
The rial traded at around 2.7 million to the dollar on the unofficial market in the past week, compared with about 1.7 million before the war.
The minimum monthly wage that stood at around US$120 a year ago has fallen to US$65.
The country's economy minister has rejected predictions of an imminent economic collapse, accusing Iran's foes of trying to fuel public anxiety and drive up exchange rates.
Prices 'skyrocketed'
Azadeh offers a price comparison of a kitchen cloth bought several months ago for 22 cents. She says that item now costs US$1.10, five times more.
"It shows that prices haven't just gone up -- they've truly skyrocketed," she said.
She has stopped buying some fruits and says she can no longer afford holidays.
"We aren't meant to just exist, we're meant to actually live, right?" she asked.
Car mechanic Mojtaba Rezaei says his customers have "dropped to a tenth of what it was" because "goods now cost two or three times as much".
"I actually feel embarrassed telling prices to customers. People just come in, ask the price, and leave," the 57-year-old told AFP at the bazaar.
"So many things -- buying clothes, going out for leisure, dining at restaurants -- have all been cut out of our lives."
02be7e1328b8d896: PETALING JAYA: The royal and customary crisis in Negeri Sembilan has had no bearing on PAS’s efforts to work with Umno in the Melaka state election, despite the potential political fallout for both parties, says an analyst.

Yesterday, PAS president Abdul Hadi Awang said PAS and BN had reached an agreement in principle to cooperate in the Nov 14 Melaka state election. However, seat allocation and candidate selection were still being discussed.
PAS's Serting assemblyman Fairuz Isa was a member of the Negeri Sembilan state executive council under Ismail Lasim.

His appointment and those of nine other exco members were revoked on Sept 21 by Negeri Sembilan ruler Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir after they declared his removal in April legitimate and recognised Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Jaafar as the new ruler.

f3448035831ea3e4: PANAMA CITY: Panama mengisytiharkan keadaan darurat pada Sabtu bagi menyelaraskan usaha bantuan dan membantu komuniti terjejas akibat gempa bumi kuat yang melanda negara itu pada Jumaat, lapor Xinhua.

Menteri Kepresidenan, Juan Carlos Orillac, pada sidang media di istana presiden berkata pengisytiharan itu akan memastikan agensi kerajaan sentiasa bersiap siaga dan mempunyai sumber diperlukan untuk membantu penduduk terjejas.
Katanya, Presiden Jose Raul Mulino mengarahkan penubuhan sebuah jawatankuasa bagi menyelaras operasi bantuan, mengurus sumber serta menangani keperluan komuniti terjejas.
Beliau berkata, kerajaan turut menubuhkan pusat pengumpulan sumbangan, termasuk di Omar Park di Panama City, manakala pejabat kerajaan wilayah akan dijadikan pusat pengumpulan tambahan.
Gempa bumi bermagnitud 7.5 melanda Panama pada 12.56 tengah hari Jumaat (waktu tempatan), dengan pusat gempa terletak kira-kira 39km ke barat laut Tonosi di wilayah Los Santos.
Gempa bumi itu merosakkan rumah, sekolah, kemudahan kesihatan, jalan raya dan bangunan awam di beberapa kawasan di seluruh negara.
Pihak berkuasa Panama terus menilai kerosakan dan menyelaras usaha tindak balas kecemasan.
ce778fec24c53bd0: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 11 — There are no reports of Malaysian casualties resulting from the latest attack on Saudi Arabia’s King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and a projectile falling in the vicinity of King Fahd International Airport in Dammam on Saturday, the Foreign Ministry said.

In a statement, the ministry also known as Wisma Putra, said the Embassy of Malaysia in Riyadh was in contact with several Malaysians stranded by the travel disruptions and was providing the necessary consular assistance.
“Malaysians residing in, travelling through, or planning to travel to Saudi Arabia are strongly urged to remain vigilant.

“In view of the ongoing flight disruptions, those with upcoming travel plans are advised to verify their flight status directly with their respective airlines before proceeding to the airports,” it said in the statement issued on Sunday.
The ministry also advised Malaysians to anticipate possible delays or cancellations, stay informed through official channels and strictly adhere to safety instructions issued by local authorities.
Following the incident, Saudi Arabia’s General Authority of Civil Aviation announced the temporary suspension of operations at King Khalid International Airport.

To ensure timely communication and access to consular support, Wisma Putra urged Malaysians to register and regularly update their contact details via the e-Konsular portal at https://ekonsular.kln.gov.my.

For immediate consular assistance or emergencies, Malaysians may contact the Embassy of Malaysia in Riyadh at 00 966 11 488 7098/ 00 966 11 488 7100 for general enquiries, or the emergency helpline at 00 966 56 300 6319 after office hours, or via email mwriyadh@kln.gov.my.
Wisma Putra said it will continue to monitor the developments closely and provide further updates as necessary.
In a statement on Sunday, the Saudi General Authority of Civil Aviation said 12 people were killed and 309 injured in Saturday’s attack on the King Khalid International Airport.
Four Saudi citizens, two Bangladeshi nationals, and one each from the US, Egypt, Jordan, Syria, Palestine, and Sudan were killed in the attack. — Bernama
b658c4bce2ead1ad: PETALING JAYA: Johor remains the hardest hit by haze, with eight areas continuing to record unhealthy air pollutant index (API) readings this morning.
However, the overall situation nationwide has improved, with a total of only 14 areas recording unhealthy API readings as of 10am.
The eight Johor areas were Pasir Gudang with an API reading of 179, Larkin 178, Kota Tinggi 165, Tangkak 163, Segamat 161, Pengerang 160, Kluang 159 and Batu Pahat 145.
Terengganu has three areas badly affected by the haze. They are Kuala Terengganu with 157, Kemaman 156 and Paka 144.
In Pahang, two areas recorded unhealthy API readings - Balok Baru Kuantan 159 and Rompin 152.
Cheras in Kuala Lumpur is the only place affected in the Klang Valley, with a reading of 156, as Selangor, Negeri Sembilan and Perak reported moderate readings in all areas.
Yesterday, the Johor government ordered schools and other educational institutions in the state to remain closed for five more days from Monday due to deteriorating air quality across the state.
An API reading between 101 and 200 is classified as unhealthy, while readings above 200 are considered very unhealthy.
2c20e62839878167: PETALING JAYA: Sebanyak 14 kawasan di seluruh negara mencatatkan bacaan indeks pencemaran udara (IPU) tidak sihat setakat 10 pagi ini, dengan lapan daripadanya terletak di Johor.

Kawasan lain dengan IPU tidak sihat ialah Kuala Terengganu (157), Kemaman (156) dan Paka (144) di Terengganu serta Cheras di Kuala Lumpur (156).

Sebanyak 50 kawasan mencatatkan bacaan IPU sederhana dan empat kawasan dengan kualiti udara baik, iaitu Minden di Pulau Pinang (49), Kangar di Perlis (47), Langkawi di Kedah (37) dan Balik Pulau Pinang di Pulau Pinang (25).
